docs.title: 58 AI Agents on Your Own Computer
docs.text:
Learn how AI agents work by reading and running 58 small, complete examples, all on free local models with Ollama. No API keys, no cloud bills.

Each agent is one short Python file plus a README that explains the idea behind it: what it does, the concepts it teaches, how the code flows, how to run it, things to try, and its honest limits.

  • 58 agents

    50 core agents across five frameworks, plus 8 extras: the plain Anthropic SDK, MCP, A2A, a REST API, a bank-statement analyst and a stock-portfolio watcher.

  • 5 frameworks, side by side

    LangGraph (14), CrewAI (12), Agno (10), AutoGen (9) and LlamaIndex (5). Several ideas are built in more than one framework, so you can compare them.

  • Runs locally

    Every agent was run and checked on a 7B model (qwen2.5:7b-instruct) through Ollama. Your data never leaves your machine.

  • Honest about failure

    Small models make mistakes. Each README records what went wrong in testing and how the code was changed to fix it. Those lessons are the most valuable part.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: You need about 10 minutes, roughly 10 GB of free disk space, and ideally a GPU with 8 GB or more of memory (a CPU works, just slower).

docs.title: 1. Install Ollama and the models
docs.text:
Install Ollama from ollama.com, then pull the models the agents use:

ollama pull qwen2.5:7b-instruct        # main model for all agents (good at tool calling)
ollama pull qwen3-embedding            # embeddings for the RAG agents
ollama pull qwen3-coder:30b            # optional: only agents 04 and 45 (code generation)
ollama pull qwen2.5:14b-instruct       # optional: a stronger model to compare with

Check it works:

ollama run qwen2.5:7b-instruct "Say hi"

Why qwen2.5 and not llama3.1?

In testing, llama3.1:8b printed its tool calls as plain text instead of actually calling the tools. qwen2.5:7b-instruct handles tool calling reliably at the same size.

docs.title: 2. Get the code
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/rahulsing/50-agents-for-all.git
cd 50-agents-for-all

docs.title: 3. Create one Python environment per framework
docs.text:
The frameworks need different versions of the same libraries, so each gets its own virtual environment. Python 3.12 is recommended (some frameworks don't support 3.13+ yet). The examples use uv, which is fast; plain python -m venv + pip works too.

WindowsmacOS / Linux 
uv venv .venv-agno --python 3.12
uv pip install --python .venv-agno\Scripts\python.exe -r agno\01_research_agent\requirements.txt

uv venv .venv-agno --python 3.12
uv pip install --python .venv-agno/bin/python -r agno/01_research_agent/requirements.txt

Repeat for the frameworks you want: .venv-langgraph, .venv-crewai, .venv-autogen, .venv-llamaindex (use any agent's requirements.txt in that framework's folder; all agents of a framework share one environment). The protocol extras use the Agno or LangGraph environment, as their pages say.

docs.title: 4. Run your first agent
docs.text:
WindowsmacOS / Linux 
.venv-agno\Scripts\python.exe agno\01_research_agent\main.py "What is retrieval augmented generation?"

.venv-agno/bin/python agno/01_research_agent/main.py "What is retrieval augmented generation?"

You should see the tool calls (web searches) and then a 5-bullet answer with sources.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix An agent hangs for minutes Run agents one at a time. Two programs asking the same model for different context sizes make Ollama reload it again and again. If Ollama stops answering, restart it. ModuleNotFoundError You are using the wrong environment: each framework has its own .venv-<framework>. Web search returns nothing Free search endpoints are rate-limited; wait a minute. The shared search tool already retries other backends. Emoji errors on the Windows console Already handled in the CrewAI agents; for others run set PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8. Very slow first run Models load into memory on first use, and the RAG agents embed their documents once.

docs.title: Guardrails
docs.text:
A guardrail checks what goes into or comes out of a model, and blocks, cleans or retries when a rule is broken. Three agents show each framework's built-in guardrail feature; several others use hand-written guardrails, plain code that stops a small model's typical mistakes.

In every agent's code, search for GUARDRAIL to jump to the relevant lines.

docs.title: Framework built-in guardrails
docs.text: Agent Framework feature What it guards 39 Support Agent Agno pre_hooks with PromptInjectionGuardrail and PIIDetectionGuardrail, plus a custom post_hooks check Blocks prompt-injection messages and card/IBAN/SSN numbers before the model is called; blocks replies that contain card-like numbers or leak instructions 09 Job Posting Generator CrewAI Task(guardrails=[function, "plain-English rule"], guardrail_max_retries=3) Length, biased wording, required sections and invented salaries (code); discriminatory requirements (checked by an LLM). Failures go back to the agent for a rewrite 31 Supervisor Multi-Agent LangChain middleware PIIMiddleware, ModelCallLimitMiddleware, ToolCallLimitMiddleware, plus a PII node at the graph's entry Redacts emails and masks card numbers for the whole team; caps model and tool calls per worker

    model=...,
    pre_hooks=[PromptInjectionGuardrail(), PIIDetectionGuardrail(enable_email_check=False)],
    post_hooks=[output_guardrail],   # your own function; raise OutputCheckError to block
)

    print("Blocked:", run.content)

def posting_rules(result: TaskOutput) -> tuple[bool, Any]:
    if len(result.raw.split()) > 450:
        return False, "Too long: shorten About us to 2 sentences ..."   # feedback for the retry
    return True, result

                               "The posting must not contain requirements based on age or gender ..."],
              guardrail_max_retries=3)

researcher = create_agent(llm, [web_search], middleware=[
    PIIMiddleware("email", strategy="redact"),
    PIIMiddleware("credit_card", strategy="mask"),
    ModelCallLimitMiddleware(run_limit=5, exit_behavior="end"),
    ToolCallLimitMiddleware(tool_name="web_search", run_limit=2),
])

docs.title: Hand-written guardrails
docs.text: Agent Guardrail 21 SQL Agent, 25 NL to SQL The database is opened read-only and only SELECT queries are accepted 25 NL to SQL VerifiedApproval: an approval only counts if its numbers appear together in a real query result row 31 Supervisor, 47 Collaboration Workflow order enforced in the router: the analyst must check the numbers before the run can finish 39 Support Agent The model only decides to escalate; code opens the ticket, and only with a real email from the message 23 Recruitment, 43 Lead Score Scores are computed in code from the model's yes/no judgements 48 Chess A referee in code validates every proposed move 04 Code Loop, 45 Code Assistant Model-written code runs in a separate process with a timeout

docs.title: What testing taught about guardrails
docs.text:
• Too broad means blocked forever. A "no salary" rule matching any currency amount rejected "customer deposits of £25 billion" on every retry.
  • Feedback must be actionable. "Under 450 words" got the same 473-word text back each time; "shorten About us to 2 sentences, at most 4 bullets per section" worked.
  • LLM guardrails are not deterministic. The fairness rule caught "under 30, male preferred", but once also rejected a clean posting. Put hard rules in code; use LLM guardrails for judgement.
  • Protect the whole system, not just one agent. LangChain's PII middleware cleans only the last user message; in a multi-agent graph other agents still saw the raw email and card number until the input was cleaned at the graph's entry.
  • Blocked inputs are cheap. A blocked message never reaches the model, so the answer comes back in about 3 seconds instead of 20.

docs.text:

Want to see what all of them hide? Read 51: the same research agent with no framework at all. The whole "agent" is a 20-line loop.

docs.title: Shared code
docs.text: A few helpers are shared by many agents, in the common/ folder: model names, a web-search tool with fallbacks, a safe calculator, and one small setup helper per framework. See Shared code.

docs.title: Reading tips
docs.text:
• Read the Known limits first. They show where small models fail and which code patterns fixed it.
  • Run the agent, then try one item from Things to try. Changing one line teaches more than reading ten.
  • Compare the same idea in two frameworks, for example SQL agents 21 (LangGraph) and 25 (AutoGen), or research agents 01, 15 and 51.

docs.title: Lessons learned: making small local models reliable
docs.text: Every agent here was run against a 7B model, and many failed the first time in instructive ways. These are the patterns that fixed them. Each links to the agent where it happened.

docs.title: 1. Let the model decide; let code act and calculate
docs.text:
Small models are good at judgement and language, bad at arithmetic and at following procedures exactly.

  • Scores: asked for a 0-100 score, a model gave a candidate missing half the requirements 85/100, and another answered on a 0-10 scale so no lead ever passed the threshold. Fix: the model judges each criterion (yes/no + evidence); code computes the score. (23, 43)
  • Maths: totals, rankings and "best/worst month" are computed in Python; the model only explains them. (57, 58)
  • Side effects: a support agent with a create_ticket tool invented email addresses and even ticket numbers. Fix: the model returns escalate: true, and code opens the ticket only with a real email from the message. (39)

docs.title: 2. Verify claims against real tool output
docs.text:
• A reviewer agent wrote correct SQL, then typed an imaginary result table instead of running it and approved its own invented numbers. Fix: a termination condition that accepts an approval only if its numbers appear in a real query result. (25)
  • A planner returned an empty list of questions and silently answered from memory instead of calling the remote agent. Fix: fall back to sending the whole goal. (55)

docs.title: 3. Enforce the workflow in code when prompts are ignored
docs.text:
• A researcher kept doing the maths itself and finishing early, so the analyst with the calculator never ran, even when told not to. Fix: a rule in the router: only the analyst may finish. (31, 47)
  • Chess players skipped their move tools and just typed moves as chat. Fix: code runs the game loop, shows the legal moves, and validates every move. (48)

docs.title: 4. Give the model the context; don't make it explore
docs.text:
• A README generator listed the wrong folder, got nothing, and invented a whole project. Fix: code lists the files and puts them in the prompt. (34)
  • An SQL agent guessed column names before reading the schema. Fix: put the schema in the system prompt. (25)

docs.title: 5. One document (or clause) per call
docs.text:
• Asked to review a whole contract in one structured reply, the model returned an empty clause list. Split by clause, it reviewed every one. (22)
  • CVs are screened one per task. (23)

docs.title: 6. Keep structured outputs small
docs.text: • Asking for a long answer plus a critique in one JSON object made the model emit whitespace for 20+ minutes, blocking Ollama for every other program. With a length cap, the JSON was cut off instead. Fix: write the answer as plain text; only the short critique is structured. (35)

docs.title: 7. Guardrails need care too
docs.text:
• A salary rule that matched any currency amount rejected "customer deposits of £25 billion" on every retry. (09)
  • "Cut it to under 450 words" produced the same text each retry: small models can't count. Feedback must say what to change.
  • LangChain's PII middleware only cleans the last user message; in a multi-agent graph the original message still reached other agents. Fix: clean the input once at the graph's entry. (31)

See all of them on the Guardrails page.

docs.title: 8. Running models locally
docs.text:
• Context size: qwen3-coder:30b defaults to a 262k-token context; loaded that way it spilled onto the CPU and blocked Ollama. Set num_ctx (e.g. 16384) for such models. CrewAI talks to Ollama through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which can't set it, so CrewAI agents use the 7B model.
  • Mixed context sizes: different programs requesting the same model with different num_ctx force constant reloads; under load Ollama stalled. Use the same size everywhere and run tests one at a time.
  • Tool calling varies by model: llama3.1:8b printed tool calls as text; qwen2.5:7b-instruct executed them.
  • Free web search is flaky: the shared web_search retries several backends.

docs.title: 9. Library details that cost time
docs.text: Library Gotcha Agno 3.x The Ollama model needs the openai package; SqliteDb needs greenlet; MCPTools needs fastmcp; a guardrail stop returns status == error instead of raising LangGraph / LangChain 1.x create_agent lives in langchain.agents; the in-memory vector store needs numpy CrewAI 1.x result.raw is only the last task (use tasks_output); the console needs UTF-8 on Windows AutoGen 0.7 Local models need an explicit model_info; small models write TERMINATE in the same message as code LlamaIndex SubQuestionQueryEngine needs LLMQuestionGenerator without the OpenAI package; context_window is sent to Ollama as num_ctx MCP SDK 2.x renamed FastMCP to MCPServer A2A a2a-sdk 1.x uses protobuf types and route helpers; older tutorials' A2AStarletteApplication is gone; raise the client timeout

docs.title: Shared code
docs.text:
Helpers in common/ used by many agents. Every agent imports model names from common/llm.py, so you can switch models in one place.

common/autogen_client.py
"""AutoGen model client for local Ollama models."""
from autogen_ext.models.ollama import OllamaChatCompletionClient

from common.llm import OLLAMA_URL


def ollama_client(model: str, tools: bool = True, temperature: float = 0.0) -> OllamaChatCompletionClient:
    # AutoGen only knows capabilities of models it recognises, so local models need an explicit model_info
    return OllamaChatCompletionClient(
        model=model,
        host=OLLAMA_URL,
        # No num_ctx here: every framework should use Ollama's default context for the same model, otherwise
        # concurrent requests with different sizes force Ollama to reload the model again and again
        options={"temperature": temperature},
        model_info={"vision": False, "function_calling": tools, "json_output": True,
                    "family": "unknown", "structured_output": True},
    )
common/crewai_env.py
"""Import this BEFORE crewai: disables telemetry and makes the Windows console print CrewAI's emoji safely."""
import os
import sys

os.environ.setdefault("CREWAI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY", "true")
os.environ.setdefault("OTEL_SDK_DISABLED", "true")
for _stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
    _stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")


def ollama_llm(model: str, temperature: float = 0.3):
    """CrewAI talks to Ollama using the 'ollama/<model>' name.

    CrewAI uses Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which cannot set the context size (num_ctx) per request,
    so Ollama uses the model's default. Avoid models whose default is huge (qwen3-coder: 262k tokens) here."""
    from crewai import LLM

    from common.llm import OLLAMA_URL
    return LLM(model=f"ollama/{model}", base_url=OLLAMA_URL, temperature=temperature)

"""Point LlamaIndex at local Ollama instead of its OpenAI default."""
from llama_index.core import Settings
from llama_index.embeddings.ollama import OllamaEmbedding
from llama_index.llms.ollama import Ollama

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, EMBED_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL


def use_ollama(model: str = DEFAULT_MODEL, context_window: int = 32768) -> None:
    # LlamaIndex sends context_window to Ollama as num_ctx; 32768 matches Ollama's default for qwen2.5,
    # so all frameworks share one loaded copy of the model instead of forcing reloads
    Settings.llm = Ollama(model=model, base_url=OLLAMA_URL, request_timeout=300, temperature=0,
                          context_window=context_window)
    Settings.embed_model = OllamaEmbedding(model_name=EMBED_MODEL, base_url=OLLAMA_URL)

"""Creates a small sample shop database (SQLite) used by the SQL agents (21, 25)."""
import random
import sqlite3
from datetime import date, timedelta
from pathlib import Path


def create_shop_db(path: Path) -> Path:
    if path.exists():
        return path
    rng = random.Random(42)  # fixed seed: everyone gets the same data
    con = sqlite3.connect(path)
    cur = con.cursor()
    cur.executescript("""
        CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, city TEXT, joined DATE);
        CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, category TEXT, price REAL);
        CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER REFERENCES customers(id),
                             product_id INTEGER REFERENCES products(id), quantity INTEGER, order_date DATE);
    """)
    cities = ["London", "Paris", "Berlin", "Madrid", "Rome"]
    names = ["Alice", "Bob", "Chen", "Diana", "Emre", "Fatima", "George", "Hana", "Ivan", "Julia",
             "Kofi", "Lena", "Mateo", "Nora", "Omar"]
    for i, n in enumerate(names, 1):
        cur.execute("INSERT INTO customers VALUES (?,?,?,?)",
                    (i, n, cities[i % 5], date(2025, 1, 1) + timedelta(days=rng.randint(0, 500))))
    products = [("Laptop", "Electronics", 999), ("Headphones", "Electronics", 149), ("Monitor", "Electronics", 249),
                ("Desk", "Furniture", 320), ("Chair", "Furniture", 180), ("Lamp", "Furniture", 45),
                ("Notebook", "Stationery", 4.5), ("Pen pack", "Stationery", 7), ("Backpack", "Accessories", 65),
                ("Water bottle", "Accessories", 18)]
    for i, (n, c, p) in enumerate(products, 1):
        cur.execute("INSERT INTO products VALUES (?,?,?,?)", (i, n, c, p))
    for i in range(1, 201):
        cur.execute("INSERT INTO orders VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)",
                    (i, rng.randint(1, 15), rng.randint(1, 10), rng.randint(1, 4),
                     date(2026, 1, 1) + timedelta(days=rng.randint(0, 270))))
    con.commit()
    con.close()
    return path
common/tools.py
"""Plain-Python tool functions shared by several agents. Each framework wraps them in its own tool format."""
import ast
import operator

from ddgs import DDGS

_OPS = {ast.Add: operator.add, ast.Sub: operator.sub, ast.Mult: operator.mul, ast.Div: operator.truediv,
        ast.Pow: operator.pow, ast.Mod: operator.mod, ast.USub: operator.neg}


def web_search(query: str, max_results: int = 4) -> str:
    """Search the web with the ddgs metasearch library (no API key); returns title, snippet and URL per result.

    Free search endpoints sometimes return nothing or rate-limit, so several backends are tried in turn."""
    error = None
    for backend in ("auto", "duckduckgo", "bing", "brave"):
        try:
            results = DDGS().text(query, max_results=max_results, backend=backend)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - try the next backend, report the last error to the model
            error = e
            continue
        if results:
            return "\n".join(f"- {r['title']}: {r['body']} ({r['href']})" for r in results)
    return f"Search failed: {error or 'no results'}"


def _eval(node):
    if isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and isinstance(node.value, (int, float)):
        return node.value
    if isinstance(node, ast.BinOp) and type(node.op) in _OPS:
        return _OPS[type(node.op)](_eval(node.left), _eval(node.right))
    if isinstance(node, ast.UnaryOp) and type(node.op) in _OPS:
        return _OPS[type(node.op)](_eval(node.operand))
    raise ValueError("only numbers and + - * / ** % are allowed")


def calculate(expression: str) -> str:
    """Safely evaluate an arithmetic expression such as '(1200 * 0.15) / 3' (no eval of arbitrary code)."""
    try:
        return str(_eval(ast.parse(expression.replace(",", ""), mode="eval").body))
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return f"Error: {e}"

docs.title: Agent 01 - Research Agent (Agno)
docs.text: Framework: Agno  ·  Industry: Research  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: You ask a question. The agent searches the web with DuckDuckGo, then answers in 5 bullets and lists the source URLs.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Agent = model + tools + instructions. This is the whole agent; there is no graph or crew.
  • Tool calling: the model does not search by itself. It emits a request ("call web_search with query X"), the framework runs the tool, and the result goes back to the model, which then writes the answer.
  • Instructions steer format (5 bullets, sources at the end) without any extra code.

docs.title: How the code works (main.py)
docs.text:
1. Ollama(id=DEFAULT_MODEL, host=OLLAMA_URL) connects Agno to your local Ollama.
  2. DuckDuckGoTools() gives the agent two tools: web_search and search_news. No API key needed.
  3. instructions=[...] is the system prompt, as a list of rules.
  4. debug_mode=True prints each tool call so you can see the agent really searched.
  5. print_response(question) runs the agent and prints the answer.
question -> model -> "call web_search" -> DuckDuckGo -> results -> model -> 5 bullets + sources

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class Recipe(BaseModel):
    name: str
    servings: int
    prep_minutes: int = Field(description="Total time in minutes")
    ingredients: list[str] = Field(description="Each item with a quantity, e.g. '2 eggs'")
    steps: list[str]
    uses_only_given: bool = Field(description="True if no main ingredients beyond the given ones (pantry staples allowed)")


def build_agent() -> Agent:
    return Agent(
        model=Ollama(id=DEFAULT_MODEL, host=OLLAMA_URL),
        instructions=[
            "You are a home cook. Create one recipe from the ingredients the user has.",
            "You may add pantry staples: salt, pepper, oil, butter, water, flour, sugar, common spices.",
            "Respect any dietary need the user states.",
        ],
        output_schema=Recipe,
    )


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Agno recipe creator with structured output")
    p.add_argument("ingredients", nargs="?", default="")

        sys.exit(2)
    print(f"\n# {r.name}\nServes {r.servings} | {r.prep_minutes} min | only given ingredients: {r.uses_only_given}\n")
    print("## Ingredients")
    print("\n".join(f"- {i}" for i in r.ingredients))
    print("\n## Steps")
    print("\n".join(f"{n}. {s}" for n, s in enumerate(r.steps, 1)))


if __name__ == "__main__":

from agno.db.sqlite import SqliteDb
from agno.models.ollama import Ollama

        model=Ollama(id=DEFAULT_MODEL, host=OLLAMA_URL),
        db=SqliteDb(db_file=str(DB_FILE)),
        session_id=session,
        add_history_to_context=True,  # earlier turns of this session are sent with each new message
        num_history_runs=8,
        instructions=[
            f"You are a patient study partner for the topic: {topic}.",
            "Explain simply, with one short example. Keep answers under 150 words.",
            "When the user says 'quiz me', ask ONE multiple-choice question (A-D) and wait for the answer.",
            "When the user answers a quiz, say if it is right, explain why, and keep score across the session.",
        ],
        markdown=True,
    )


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Agno study partner with session memory")
    p.add_argument("topic", nargs="?", default="")
    p.add_argument("--session", default="default", help="same name = continue an earlier session")

agno/22_legal_document_analysis/main.py
import argparse
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from agno.agent import Agent
from agno.models.ollama import Ollama
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL

DEFAULT_DOC = Path(__file__).parent / "docs" / "sample_service_agreement.txt"


class Clause(BaseModel):
    title: str = Field(description="Clause name, e.g. 'Liability'")
    summary: str = Field(description="One plain-English sentence")
    risk_for_reviewer: Literal["low", "medium", "high"]
    reason: str = Field(description="Why this risk level, one sentence")


class Overview(BaseModel):
    parties: list[str]
    contract_type: str
    top_concerns: list[str] = Field(description="The 3 most important issues to negotiate, one sentence each")


def split_clauses(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Split on lines that start with a clause number like '1.' so the model reviews one clause at a time."""
    parts = re.split(r"\n(?=\d+\.\s)", text)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if re.match(r"\d+\.\s", p.strip())]


def make_agent(schema: type[BaseModel], side: str) -> Agent:
    return Agent(
        model=Ollama(id=DEFAULT_MODEL, host=OLLAMA_URL),
        instructions=[
            f"You review contracts on behalf of the {side}. Judge risk from the {side}'s point of view.",
            "Use only the given text; do not invent terms.",
        ],
        output_schema=schema,
    )


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Agno contract clause analyser")
    p.add_argument("file", nargs="?", default=str(DEFAULT_DOC))
    p.add_argument("--side", default="Client", help="which party you represent")
    a = p.parse_args()
    path = Path(a.file)
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip() if path.is_file() else ""
    if not text:
        print(f"File not found or empty: {path}")
        sys.exit(1)
    clauses = split_clauses(text)
    if not clauses:
        print("No numbered clauses found (expected lines starting with '1.', '2.', ...).")
        sys.exit(1)

    clause_agent = make_agent(Clause, a.side)
    reviewed: list[Clause] = []
    print(f"{'Clause':<24} {'Risk':<7} Summary")
    for c in clauses:
        result = clause_agent.run(f"Review this single clause:\n{c}").content
        if isinstance(result, Clause):
            reviewed.append(result)
            print(f"{result.title[:23]:<24} {result.risk_for_reviewer:<7} {result.summary}")
            print(f"{'':<32}why: {result.reason}")

    risky = "\n".join(f"- {r.title} ({r.risk_for_reviewer}): {r.reason}" for r in reviewed)
    overview = make_agent(Overview, a.side).run(f"Contract:\n{text[:1500]}\n\nClause risks:\n{risky}").content
    if isinstance(overview, Overview):
        print(f"\nParties: {', '.join(overview.parties)} | Type: {overview.contract_type} | Reviewing for: {a.side}")
        print("\nTop concerns:")
        print("\n".join(f"- {t}" for t in overview.top_concerns))
    print(f"\nReviewed {len(reviewed)} of {len(clauses)} clauses. Not legal advice; have a lawyer review real contracts.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from agno.agent import Agent
from agno.models.ollama import Ollama

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL

CATALOG = json.loads((Path(__file__).parent / "catalog.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def search_products(category: str, max_price: float = 100000, must_have: str = "") -> str:
    """Search the store catalog.

    Args:
        category: product category: headphones, laptop or kettle
        max_price: highest price in USD the user accepts
        must_have: optional feature that must appear, e.g. 'noise cancelling'
    """
    cat = category.lower().strip()
    hits = [
        p for p in CATALOG
        if p["category"] in (cat, cat.rstrip("s"))
        and p["price"] <= float(max_price)
        and (not must_have or any(must_have.lower() in f for f in p["features"]))
    ]
    return json.dumps(hits) if hits else "No products match."


def get_product(product_id: str) -> str:
    """Get full details of one product by its id, e.g. H1."""
    for p in CATALOG:
        if p["id"] == product_id.upper():
            return json.dumps(p)
    return "Unknown product id."


def build_agent() -> Agent:
    return Agent(
        model=Ollama(id=DEFAULT_MODEL, host=OLLAMA_URL),
        tools=[search_products, get_product],  # plain functions: Agno builds each tool schema from the docstring
        instructions=[
            "You are a shopping assistant for this store only. Use search_products; never invent products.",
            "Recommend at most 3 products in a markdown table (name, price, rating, why it fits).",
            "Then name your single top pick and one trade-off. If nothing fits, say so and suggest relaxing a filter.",
        ],
        markdown=True,
        debug_mode=True,
    )


def main() -> None:
    request = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]).strip()
    if not request:
        print('Please describe what you want, e.g. main.py "noise cancelling headphones under 200 dollars"')
        sys.exit(1)
    build_agent().print_response(request)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

agno/29_movie_recommendation/main.py
import argparse
import csv
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from agno.agent import Agent
from agno.db.sqlite import SqliteDb
from agno.models.ollama import Ollama

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL

HERE = Path(__file__).parent
with open(HERE / "movies.csv", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    MOVIES = list(csv.DictReader(f))


def search_movies(genre: str = "", max_runtime_min: int = 999, min_rating: float = 0) -> str:
    """Search the movie list.

    Args:
        genre: one genre, e.g. sci-fi, comedy, thriller, drama, animation, horror, romance, action
        max_runtime_min: longest acceptable runtime in minutes
        min_rating: lowest acceptable rating out of 10
    """
    hits = [
        m for m in MOVIES
        if (not genre or genre.lower() in m["genres"])
        and int(m["runtime_min"]) <= int(max_runtime_min)
        and float(m["rating"]) >= float(min_rating)
    ]
    return json.dumps(hits) if hits else "No movies match."


def build_agent(user: str) -> Agent:
    return Agent(
        model=Ollama(id=DEFAULT_MODEL, host=OLLAMA_URL),
        tools=[search_movies],
        db=SqliteDb(db_file=str(HERE / "movie_memory.db")),
        user_id=user,
        session_id=f"movies-{user}",  # same session every run, so past likes are remembered
        add_history_to_context=True,
        num_history_runs=10,
        instructions=[
            "ALWAYS call search_movies before answering, even if you know other movies.",
            "Recommend ONLY titles that search_movies returned. Never recommend a movie that is not in the results.",
            "Use what the user told you in earlier messages (likes, dislikes, movies already seen).",
            "Never recommend a movie the user said they have seen, already got from you, or disliked.",
            "Give 3 picks: title (year), one line on why it fits their taste.",
        ],
        markdown=True,
        debug_mode=True,
    )


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Agno movie recommender that remembers you between runs")
    p.add_argument("message", nargs="?", default="")
    p.add_argument("--user", default="me")
    p.add_argument("--forget", action="store_true", help="delete the memory file and start fresh")
    a = p.parse_args()
    if a.forget:
        (HERE / "movie_memory.db").unlink(missing_ok=True)
        print("Memory cleared.")
        return
    if not a.message.strip():
        print('Please say what you like, e.g. main.py "I loved Inception, recommend something"')
        sys.exit(1)
    build_agent(a.user).print_response(a.message.strip())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from agno.agent import Agent
from agno.models.ollama import Ollama
from agno.tools.file import FileTools

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL


def build_agent(project: Path) -> Agent:
    return Agent(
        model=Ollama(id=DEFAULT_MODEL, host=OLLAMA_URL),
        # Read-only file access, sandboxed to the project folder
        tools=[FileTools(base_dir=project, enable_save_file=False, enable_delete_file=False,
                         enable_replace_file_chunk=False, enable_read_file=True, enable_list_files=True,
                         enable_search_files=True)],
        instructions=[
            "You write README.md files for code projects.",
            "You are given the file list. Read the main source files (at most 4) with read_file before writing; "
            "paths are relative to the project root.",
            "If you cannot read the files, say so instead of guessing. Never invent files, libraries or commands.",
            "Write these sections: title and one-line description, Features, Requirements, "
            "How to run (exact commands from the code), Project structure, Notes.",
            "Only describe what you saw in the files. Output only the README markdown.",
        ],
        debug_mode=True,
    )


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Agno README generator")
    p.add_argument("project", nargs="?", default="")
    p.add_argument("--out", help="save the README here instead of only printing it")
    a = p.parse_args()
    project = Path(a.project).resolve() if a.project else None
    if not project or not project.is_dir():
        print("Please give a project folder, e.g. main.py ..\\26_shopping_partner")
        sys.exit(1)
    skip = {".db", ".pyc", ".lance", ".png", ".jpg"}
    files = sorted(str(f.relative_to(project)) for f in project.rglob("*")
                   if f.is_file() and f.suffix not in skip and "__pycache__" not in f.parts)[:40]
    prompt = f"Project folder name: {project.name}\nFiles (relative to the root):\n" + "\n".join(files)
    readme = build_agent(project).run(prompt + "\n\nRead the key files, then write the README.").content
    print(readme)
    if a.out:
        Path(a.out).write_text(readme, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"\nSaved to {a.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Agent 39 - Support Agent (Agno)
docs.text:
Framework: Agno  ·  Industry: Customer Service  ·  Source folder on GitHub

Guardrails

This agent demonstrates guardrails. Search the code below for GUARDRAIL, and see the Guardrails overview.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Customer support for a fictional app (CloudNote). It answers from a help-center knowledge base and names the section it used. If the help center cannot solve the problem (or the customer already tried those steps), it opens a ticket in tickets.json using the email in the customer's message.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Agno Knowledge + vector DB: Knowledge(vector_db=LanceDb(...)) embeds kb/faq.md once with Ollama embeddings and stores it on disk in lancedb/. add_knowledge_to_context=True retrieves the relevant text for every message.
  • The model decides, code acts: earlier versions gave the model a create_ticket tool. The 7B model created tickets with made-up emails and even invented ticket ids without calling the tool; a 14B model called the tool but answered in Thai. The working design returns a structured SupportReply with an escalate flag, and plain Python creates the ticket only if there is a real email in the customer's message.
  • Why this matters: for actions with side effects (tickets, refunds, emails), keep the final action in code you control.

docs.title: Guardrails (Agno built-in)
docs.text:
Search main.py for GUARDRAIL to find them.

Guardrail Type When it runs What it does PromptInjectionGuardrail() Agno built-in, pre_hooks before the model Blocks messages like "ignore your instructions", "developer mode", "jailbreak" PIIDetectionGuardrail(...) Agno built-in, pre_hooks before the model Blocks card numbers, US SSNs and IBANs (custom pattern). Emails and phone numbers are allowed because the ticket flow needs an email output_guardrail custom function, post_hooks after the model Rejects a reply containing a card-like number or leaked internal instructions

When a guardrail fires, Agno stops the run and returns it with status == RunStatus.error (it does not raise), so main.py checks the status and prints a safe message (exit code 3). A blocked input never reaches the model, which also saves time.

docs.title: The flow
docs.text:
message -> retrieve help-center text -> model -> SupportReply {answer, section, escalate}
                                              -> escalate and email found? -> create ticket (code)

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
agno/39_support_agent/main.py
import json
import re
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from agno.agent import Agent
from agno.exceptions import CheckTrigger, OutputCheckError
from agno.guardrails import PIIDetectionGuardrail, PromptInjectionGuardrail
from agno.knowledge.embedder.ollama import OllamaEmbedder
from agno.knowledge.knowledge import Knowledge
from agno.models.ollama import Ollama
from agno.run.agent import RunOutput
from agno.run.base import RunStatus
from agno.vectordb.lancedb import LanceDb, SearchType
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, EMBED_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL

HERE = Path(__file__).parent
TICKETS = HERE / "tickets.json"
EMBED_DIMS = 4096  # qwen3-embedding output size; change if you change EMBED_MODEL
EMAIL = re.compile(r"[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[a-z]{2,}", re.I)

# ----- GUARDRAILS ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Input guardrails run as pre_hooks, BEFORE the model sees the message. If one raises, the run stops and the
# model is never called. These two are Agno's built-in guardrails (agno.guardrails).
INPUT_GUARDRAILS = [
    PromptInjectionGuardrail(),  # blocks "ignore your instructions", "developer mode", "jailbreak", ...
    PIIDetectionGuardrail(
        enable_email_check=False,  # emails are allowed: the support flow needs one to open a ticket
        enable_phone_check=False,
        custom_patterns={"IBAN": r"\b[A-Z]{2}\d{2}(?:\s?[A-Z0-9]{4}){3,7}\b"},  # bank account numbers
    ),  # blocks card numbers, US SSNs and IBANs: customers must never send these to a support bot
]
LEAK_MARKERS = ("help-center references", "<references>", "system prompt", "instructions:")


def output_guardrail(run_output: RunOutput) -> None:
    """Custom output guardrail (a post_hook): runs AFTER the model answers, BEFORE the reply is used.

    Blocks replies that contain a card-like number or leak the agent's internal instructions."""
    text = str(run_output.content)
    if re.search(r"\b\d{4}[\s-]?\d{4}[\s-]?\d{4}[\s-]?\d{4}\b", text):
        raise OutputCheckError("Reply contained a card-like number", check_trigger=CheckTrigger.OUTPUT_NOT_ALLOWED)
    if any(marker in text.lower() for marker in LEAK_MARKERS):
        raise OutputCheckError("Reply leaked internal instructions", check_trigger=CheckTrigger.OUTPUT_NOT_ALLOWED)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class SupportReply(BaseModel):
    answer: str = Field(description="Reply to the customer, based on the help-center references")
    section_used: str = Field(description="Help-center section the answer came from, or 'none'")
    escalate: bool = Field(description="True only if the references do not solve the problem, or the customer "
                                       "says they already tried those steps")
    ticket_summary: str = Field(description="One-sentence problem summary for a human agent, empty if not escalating")


def create_ticket(email: str, summary: str) -> str:
    tickets = json.loads(TICKETS.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if TICKETS.exists() else []
    ticket = {"id": f"T{len(tickets) + 1:04d}", "email": email, "summary": summary,
              "created": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
    tickets.append(ticket)
    TICKETS.write_text(json.dumps(tickets, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    return ticket["id"]


def build_knowledge() -> Knowledge:
    knowledge = Knowledge(
        vector_db=LanceDb(
            uri=str(HERE / "lancedb"),
            table_name="help_center",
            search_type=SearchType.vector,
            embedder=OllamaEmbedder(id=EMBED_MODEL, host=OLLAMA_URL, dimensions=EMBED_DIMS),
        ),
    )
    knowledge.insert(path=str(HERE / "kb"), skip_if_exists=True)  # embeds the help center once, then reuses it
    return knowledge


def build_agent() -> Agent:
    return Agent(
        model=Ollama(id=DEFAULT_MODEL, host=OLLAMA_URL),
        knowledge=build_knowledge(),
        add_knowledge_to_context=True,  # always retrieve: relevant help-center text is added to each request
        output_schema=SupportReply,
        pre_hooks=INPUT_GUARDRAILS,  # GUARDRAIL: checks the customer's message before the model runs
        post_hooks=[output_guardrail],  # GUARDRAIL: checks the model's reply before we use it
        instructions=[
            "You are CloudNote customer support. Be brief, friendly, and reply in English.",
            "Answer only from the help-center references you are given.",
            "Compare the customer's message with the help-center steps. If the customer has ALREADY done those "
            "steps, or the references do not cover the problem, set escalate to true and do not repeat the steps.",
        ],
    )


def main() -> None:
    message = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]).strip()
    if not message:
        print('Please provide a customer message, e.g. main.py "How do I get a refund?"')
        sys.exit(1)
    run = build_agent().run(message)
    if run.status == RunStatus.error:  # a guardrail stopped the run (Agno returns the error, it doesn't raise)
        print(f"\n[guardrail] Blocked: {run.content}")
        if "PII" in str(run.content):
            print("For your security, please don't share card numbers, bank details or ID numbers here.")
        elif "injection" in str(run.content):
            print("I can only help with questions about CloudNote.")
        else:
            print("Sorry, I can't send that reply. A human agent will follow up.")
        sys.exit(3)
    reply = run.content
    if not isinstance(reply, SupportReply):
        print("The model did not return a valid reply. Try again.")
        sys.exit(2)
    print(f"\n{reply.answer}\n\n[section: {reply.section_used} | escalate: {reply.escalate}]")

    # The model only DECIDES; plain code ACTS. A ticket needs a real email from the customer's own message.
    if reply.escalate:
        found = EMAIL.search(message)
        if found:
            ticket = create_ticket(found.group(0), reply.ticket_summary or message[:120])
            print(f"I've opened ticket {ticket} for our team; we'll email {found.group(0)}.")
        else:
            print("I'd like to pass this to our team. What email address should we contact you on?")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.text: Framework: Anthropic SDK  ·  Industry: Research  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Same job as Agent 01 (Agno): web search, then a 5-bullet answer with source URLs. This version uses the plain anthropic Python SDK and no agent framework, so you can see what frameworks do for you.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• The Anthropic SDK works with Ollama. Ollama exposes an Anthropic-compatible Messages API, so you only change base_url: Anthropic(base_url="http://localhost:11434", api_key="ollama"). The key is ignored. Switching to Claude later means changing these two values and the model name.
  • The agent loop, by hand. An agent is just a loop:
  • Send messages and tool definitions to the model.
  • If stop_reason == "tool_use", run each requested tool.
  • Send the results back as tool_result blocks.
  • Repeat until the model answers with no tool request.
  • Tool schema: tools are described with a name, a description and a JSON input_schema. Compare with Agno, where DuckDuckGoTools() hides all this.

docs.title: The loop
docs.text:
question -> model --(stop_reason = tool_use)--> run web_search -> tool_result -> model -> ... -> final text
MAX_TURNS = 6 stops runaway loops.

docs.title: How the code works (main.py)
docs.text:
1. TOOLS declares one tool, web_search.
  2. web_search() calls DuckDuckGo (ddgs), no API key.
  3. research() runs the loop above, appending assistant and tool-result messages each turn.
  4. Model comes from common/llm.py (qwen2.5:7b-instruct).

docs.title: Agent 04 - Code Execution Feedback Loop (AutoGen)
docs.text: Framework: AutoGen  ·  Industry: Software Dev  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: You describe a programming task. A coder agent writes a Python script, an executor agent runs it, and the output goes back to the coder. If the script fails, the coder sees the error and fixes it. It stops when the coder confirms the output is correct.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• AutoGen model: agents talk to each other in a team; the conversation is the program.
  • RoundRobinGroupChat: agents take turns in a fixed order (coder, executor, coder, ...).
  • Self-correction through feedback: the model does not need to be right the first time, because real execution results correct it.
  • Termination conditions: a team needs a rule for when to stop. Here: coder says TERMINATE after seeing output, or a maximum number of messages.

docs.title: The loop
docs.text:
task -> coder writes code -> executor runs it -> output/error -> coder
                                 ^                                  |
                                 +------- fix and resend ----------+
stop when coder replies TERMINATE (without code) or the message limit is hit

docs.title: How the code works (main.py)
docs.text:
1. OllamaChatCompletionClient connects AutoGen to local Ollama (model set by CODER_MODEL in common/llm.py, default qwen3-coder:30b).
  2. AssistantAgent("coder") has a system prompt telling it to answer with one runnable script.
  3. CodeExecutorAgent("executor") extracts the code block and runs it with LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor inside workspace/.
  4. DoneAfterExecution is a small custom termination rule. Small models tend to write TERMINATE together with the code, before it has run; this rule ignores that and waits for a TERMINATE with no code in it.
  5. Console(team.run_stream(...)) prints every message so you can watch the loop.

docs.title: Safety
docs.text: The executor runs model-written code on your machine, with your user permissions, in workspace/. AutoGen prints a warning about this. Use simple tasks, read the code in the log, and do not ask for anything that deletes files or touches the network. Running it in Docker (DockerCommandLineCodeExecutor) is the safer upgrade.

import argparse
import asyncio
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from autogen_agentchat.agents import AssistantAgent, CodeExecutorAgent
from autogen_agentchat.base import TerminatedException, TerminationCondition
from autogen_agentchat.conditions import MaxMessageTermination
from autogen_agentchat.messages import BaseAgentEvent, BaseChatMessage, StopMessage
from autogen_agentchat.teams import RoundRobinGroupChat
from autogen_agentchat.ui import Console
from autogen_ext.code_executors.local import LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor
from autogen_ext.models.ollama import OllamaChatCompletionClient

from common.llm import CODER_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL

WORKDIR = Path(__file__).parent / "workspace"

SYSTEM = """You are a Python programmer. Solve the task by writing ONE complete Python script
in a ```python code block. The script must print its result. You will see the output of running it.
If it failed, fix the code and send the full corrected script again.
Only after you have SEEN the execution output and it is correct, reply with a one-line summary and the word TERMINATE.
Never write TERMINATE in the same message as code."""


class DoneAfterExecution(TerminationCondition):
    """Stop when the coder says TERMINATE in a message that has no code block.

    Small models often write TERMINATE together with the code, before it has run.
    This ignores such messages so the executor still gets a turn.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._done = False

    @property
    def terminated(self) -> bool:
        return self._done

    async def __call__(self, messages):
        if self._done:
            raise TerminatedException("Termination condition has already been reached")
        for m in messages:
            text = m.to_text()
            if m.source == "coder" and "TERMINATE" in text and "```" not in text:
                self._done = True
                return StopMessage(content="Coder confirmed the result", source="DoneAfterExecution")
        return None

    async def reset(self) -> None:
        self._done = False


async def run(task: str, max_messages: int) -> None:
    WORKDIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    model = OllamaChatCompletionClient(
        model=CODER_MODEL,
        host=OLLAMA_URL,
        temperature=0,
        options={"num_ctx": 16384},  # qwen3-coder defaults to a 262k context, far too big for most GPUs
        model_info={"vision": False, "function_calling": False, "json_output": False,
                    "family": "unknown", "structured_output": False},
    )
    coder = AssistantAgent("coder", model_client=model, system_message=SYSTEM)
    executor = CodeExecutorAgent(
        "executor", code_executor=LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor(work_dir=WORKDIR, timeout=60)
    )
    team = RoundRobinGroupChat(
        [coder, executor],
        termination_condition=DoneAfterExecution() | MaxMessageTermination(max_messages),
    )
    await Console(team.run_stream(task=task))
    await model.close()


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="AutoGen coder + executor feedback loop")
    p.add_argument("task", nargs="?", default="")
    p.add_argument("--max-messages", type=int, default=10)
    a = p.parse_args()
    if not a.task.strip():
        print('Please provide a task, e.g. main.py "Print the first 10 primes"')
        sys.exit(1)
    asyncio.run(run(a.task.strip(), a.max_messages))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Agent 10 - Currency Calculator (AutoGen)
docs.text: Framework: AutoGen  ·  Industry: Finance  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Ask currency questions in plain English ("How much is 250 USD in EUR and in INR?"). The agent calls a conversion tool once per currency pair, using live European Central Bank rates from the free Frankfurter API, and answers in a sentence.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Function calling in AutoGen 0.7: pass a plain Python function in tools=[...]. Annotated[float, "..."] type hints plus the docstring become the tool schema.
  • reflect_on_tool_use=True: after the tool runs, the model gets a second turn to turn raw tool output into a natural answer. Without it, the agent's reply is just the tool result.
  • Parallel tool calls: for two target currencies the model issues two calls in one step (visible in the ToolCallRequestEvent).
  • Graceful degradation: if the rates API is unreachable, a fallback table is used and the answer says the rate is approximate.
  • common/autogen_client.py: local models need an explicit model_info (function calling yes/no) because AutoGen does not know their capabilities.

docs.title: The flow
docs.text: question -> model -> convert_currency(250, USD, EUR) + convert_currency(250, USD, INR) -> model -> answer

import asyncio
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Annotated

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

import httpx
from autogen_agentchat.agents import AssistantAgent
from autogen_agentchat.ui import Console

from common.autogen_client import ollama_client
from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL

# Fallback rates (USD base) used when the free rates API cannot be reached
FALLBACK = {"USD": 1.0, "EUR": 0.92, "GBP": 0.79, "INR": 83.5, "JPY": 151.0, "CAD": 1.36, "AUD": 1.52, "CHF": 0.88}


def get_rate(base: str, target: str) -> tuple[float, str]:
    base, target = base.upper(), target.upper()
    try:  # Frankfurter: free, no API key, European Central Bank rates
        r = httpx.get("https://api.frankfurter.dev/v1/latest", params={"base": base, "symbols": target}, timeout=10)
        r.raise_for_status()
        data = r.json()
        return float(data["rates"][target]), f"ECB rate on {data['date']}"
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - offline or unknown currency: fall back to the table
        if base in FALLBACK and target in FALLBACK:
            return FALLBACK[target] / FALLBACK[base], "offline fallback table (approximate)"
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown currency pair {base}/{target}")


def convert_currency(amount: Annotated[float, "Amount of money to convert"],
                     from_currency: Annotated[str, "3-letter code, e.g. USD"],
                     to_currency: Annotated[str, "3-letter code, e.g. EUR"]) -> str:
    """Convert an amount between two currencies using the latest exchange rate."""
    try:
        rate, source = get_rate(from_currency, to_currency)
    except ValueError as e:
        return str(e)
    return f"{amount:,.2f} {from_currency.upper()} = {amount * rate:,.2f} {to_currency.upper()} " \
           f"(rate {rate:.4f}, {source})"


async def run(question: str) -> None:
    client = ollama_client(DEFAULT_MODEL)
    agent = AssistantAgent(
        "currency_agent",
        model_client=client,
        tools=[convert_currency],  # AutoGen turns the type hints + docstring into a tool schema
        reflect_on_tool_use=True,  # after the tool runs, the model writes a natural-language answer
        system_message="You convert currencies. Always use convert_currency; never guess rates. "
                       "For several conversions, call the tool once per pair.",
    )
    await Console(agent.run_stream(task=question))
    await client.close()


def main() -> None:
    question = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]).strip()
    if not question:
        print('Please ask a question, e.g. main.py "How much is 250 USD in EUR and in INR?"')
        sys.exit(1)
    asyncio.run(run(question))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Answers a question from the web: it searches, opens the most relevant pages, reads them, and answers in under 150 words with a Sources list.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Two cooperating tools: web_search finds candidate pages; read_page downloads a page and strips HTML down to visible text. Snippets alone are often too thin to answer accurately.

  • Simple HTML-to-text: regular expressions remove scripts, styles, navigation and tags, and the text is cut to 3000 characters to fit the context window.
  • Compare with Agent 01: same goal, different framework, and this one reads full pages.

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import httpx
from autogen_agentchat.agents import AssistantAgent
from autogen_agentchat.ui import Console

def web_search(query: str) -> str:
    """Search the web. Returns titles, snippets and URLs."""
    return _web_search(query, 5)


def read_page(url: str) -> str:
    """Download a web page and return its visible text (first 3000 characters)."""
    try:

    return text[:3000]


async def run(question: str) -> None:
    client = ollama_client(DEFAULT_MODEL)
    agent = AssistantAgent(
        "web_researcher",
        model_client=client,
        tools=[web_search, read_page],
        max_tool_iterations=4,  # allow search -> read page -> search again, then answer
        reflect_on_tool_use=True,
        system_message="Answer using the web. First web_search, then read_page on the 1-2 most relevant URLs. "

docs.text: Framework: AutoGen  ·  Industry: Agent Patterns  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Three agents (planner, researcher with web search, writer) share one conversation. A manager, itself an LLM, reads the conversation and picks who speaks next until the writer finishes with TERMINATE.

docs.title: Concepts you learn

{roles}

Conversation so far:
{history}

Rules: planner speaks first; researcher gathers facts; writer writes the final answer once facts exist.

docs.title: Agent 25 - Natural Language to SQL with a reviewer (AutoGen)
docs.text:
Framework: AutoGen  ·  Industry: Data & Analytics  ·  Source folder on GitHub

Guardrails

This agent demonstrates guardrails. Search the code below for GUARDRAIL, and see the Guardrails overview.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Ask a question about the sample shop database. A sql_writer agent writes and runs SQLite SQL; a reviewer agent independently re-runs the SQL, compares the rows with what the writer reported, and only then gives the final answer and says APPROVED.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Verification by a second agent, with its own tools: in the first version the writer guessed column names (order_id) before reading the schema, every query failed, and it then invented a result ("5 orders, $1234.50"). The reviewer could only read the writer's text, so it approved the made-up numbers. The real answer was 37 orders worth 21,109.50. Now the reviewer has run_sql too and must re-run the query: a reviewer that can't check facts can't catch fabrication.
  • Check claims against real tool output, in code: even with a tool, the reviewer once wrote the right SQL, then typed an imaginary result table instead of running it, and approved "12 orders, $10,299" (two numbers taken from different real rows). The custom VerifiedApproval termination condition now accepts APPROVED only if the numbers in the final answer appear together in one row that run_sql actually returned; otherwise the chat continues and the writer runs the corrected SQL.
  • Give context up front: the schema is put in both system prompts by code, instead of hoping the model calls get_schema first.
  • Read-only by construction: SQLite is opened with mode=ro and only SELECT/WITH queries are accepted.
  • RoundRobinGroupChat with VerifiedApproval() | MaxMessageTermination(9).

docs.title: The chat
docs.text: question -> sql_writer (run_sql, fixes errors) -> reviewer (re-runs SQL, compares) -> APPROVED or "fix this" -> ...

  • Ask a question with a trap ("orders in Paris last year" when all data is 2026).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Two agents means more calls than Agent 21; it stops after 9 messages if they never agree.
  • It can take several rounds: in a test the writer kept adding an unneeded GROUP BY (one row per customer) for 5 queries before the reviewer's correction gave the right single total.
  • The guard checks numbers, not wording: an answer with no numbers is accepted as-is.

autogen/25_nl_to_sql/main.py
import asyncio
import re
import sqlite3
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from autogen_agentchat.agents import AssistantAgent
from autogen_agentchat.base import TerminatedException, TerminationCondition
from autogen_agentchat.conditions import MaxMessageTermination
from autogen_agentchat.messages import StopMessage, ToolCallExecutionEvent
from autogen_agentchat.teams import RoundRobinGroupChat
from autogen_agentchat.ui import Console

from common.autogen_client import ollama_client
from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL
from common.sample_db import create_shop_db

DB = create_shop_db(Path(__file__).parent / "shop.db")
NUMBER = re.compile(r"\d[\d,]*\.?\d*")


def _ro():
    return sqlite3.connect(f"file:{DB}?mode=ro", uri=True)


def get_schema() -> str:
    """Return the CREATE TABLE statements for every table."""
    with _ro() as con:
        return "\n".join(r[0] for r in con.execute("SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'"))


def run_sql(sql: str) -> str:
    """Run one read-only SELECT and return up to 15 rows."""
    if not sql.strip().lower().startswith(("select", "with")):
        return "Error: only SELECT queries are allowed."
    try:
        with _ro() as con:
            cur = con.execute(sql)
            return f"{[d[0] for d in cur.description]}\n" + "\n".join(map(str, cur.fetchmany(15)))
    except sqlite3.Error as e:
        return f"SQL error: {e}"


def _numbers(text: str) -> set[float]:
    return {float(n.replace(",", "")) for n in NUMBER.findall(text) if n.replace(",", "").replace(".", "")}


class VerifiedApproval(TerminationCondition):
    """Stop only when the reviewer says APPROVED and the numbers in its answer appear together in ONE row of a
    real run_sql result.

    In testing, the reviewer wrote a correct query but then typed an imaginary result table instead of calling
    run_sql, and approved invented numbers ("12 orders, 10299") that were pieced together from two different
    real rows. This guard rejects such approvals, so the chat continues and the sql_writer gets another turn
    to actually run the corrected query."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._done = False
        self._real_rows: list[set[float]] = []

    @property
    def terminated(self) -> bool:
        return self._done

    async def __call__(self, messages):
        if self._done:
            raise TerminatedException("Termination condition has already been reached")
        for m in messages:
            if isinstance(m, ToolCallExecutionEvent):
                for result in m.content:
                    self._real_rows += [_numbers(line) for line in result.content.splitlines()[1:]]
            elif m.source == "reviewer" and "APPROVED" in m.to_text():
                claimed = _numbers(m.to_text().split("APPROVED")[0][-300:])  # numbers in the final answer
                if claimed and not any(claimed <= row for row in self._real_rows):
                    print(f"\n[guard] approval rejected: {sorted(claimed)} do not match any real run_sql row\n")
                    continue
                self._done = True
                return StopMessage(content="Approved with verified numbers", source="VerifiedApproval")
        return None

    async def reset(self) -> None:
        self._done = False
        self._real_rows = []


async def run(question: str) -> None:
    client = ollama_client(DEFAULT_MODEL)
    schema = get_schema()  # given up front: in testing the model guessed column names before reading the schema
    sql_writer = AssistantAgent(
        "sql_writer", model_client=client, tools=[run_sql], reflect_on_tool_use=True, max_tool_iterations=4,
        system_message=f"Turn the question into SQLite SQL for this schema:\n{schema}\n"
                       "Use only these column names. Call run_sql. If it returns an error, fix the SQL and call "
                       "it again. If the reviewer suggests corrected SQL, run that. Report the final SQL and copy "
                       "the result rows exactly. Never state numbers that run_sql did not return.")
    reviewer = AssistantAgent(
        "reviewer", model_client=client, tools=[run_sql], reflect_on_tool_use=True,
        system_message=f"Schema:\n{schema}\nYou verify the sql_writer's work. Check joins, filters and grouping, "
                       "and that the result has the shape the question asks for: a question about a total needs "
                       "ONE row, not one row per customer or product. If the SQL is wrong, give the corrected SQL "
                       "and ask the sql_writer to run it. You may run SQL yourself with run_sql, but never type a "
                       "result table yourself. Only if the SQL is right, give the final answer in one sentence "
                       "using numbers copied from a real run_sql result, and end with APPROVED.")
    team = RoundRobinGroupChat([sql_writer, reviewer],
                               termination_condition=VerifiedApproval() | MaxMessageTermination(9))
    await Console(team.run_stream(task=question))
    await client.close()


def main() -> None:
    question = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]).strip()
    if not question:
        print('Please ask a question, e.g. main.py "How many orders did customers in Paris place?"')
        sys.exit(1)
    asyncio.run(run(question))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: What it does

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

import numpy as np
import ollama
from autogen_agentchat.agents import AssistantAgent
from autogen_agentchat.conditions import MaxMessageTermination, TextMentionTermination
from autogen_agentchat.teams import RoundRobinGroupChat
from autogen_agentchat.ui import Console

from common.autogen_client import ollama_client
from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, EMBED_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL

DOCS = Path(__file__).parent / "docs"


class TinyVectorStore:
    """A minimal vector store: split files into paragraphs, embed them, and search by cosine similarity."""

    def __init__(self, folder: Path):
        self.client = ollama.Client(host=OLLAMA_URL)
        self.chunks = [(p.name, chunk) for p in sorted(folder.glob("*.*"))
                       for chunk in self._split(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))]
        self.vectors = self._embed([c[1] for c in self.chunks])

    @staticmethod
    def _split(text: str) -> list[str]:
        """Split on blank lines, but glue a heading-only paragraph onto the paragraph after it."""
        chunks, pending = [], ""
        for para in (p.strip() for p in text.split("\n\n")):
            if not para:
                continue
            if para.startswith("#") and "\n" not in para:  # a lone heading: keep it with the next paragraph
                pending = f"{pending}\n{para}".strip()
                continue
            chunks.append(f"{pending}\n{para}".strip())
            pending = ""
        return chunks

    def _embed(self, texts: list[str]) -> np.ndarray:
        v = np.array(self.client.embed(model=EMBED_MODEL, input=texts)["embeddings"])
        return v / np.linalg.norm(v, axis=1, keepdims=True)

    def search(self, query: str, k: int = 3) -> list[tuple[str, str, float]]:
        scores = self.vectors @ self._embed([query])[0]
        return [(*self.chunks[i], float(scores[i])) for i in np.argsort(-scores)[:k]]


STORE = TinyVectorStore(DOCS)


def search_docs(query: str) -> str:
    """Search the company documents. Returns the 3 best matching passages with their file names."""
    return "\n\n".join(f"[{name}, score {s:.2f}] {text}" for name, text, s in STORE.search(query))


async def run(question: str) -> None:
    client = ollama_client(DEFAULT_MODEL)
    retriever = AssistantAgent("retriever", model_client=client, tools=[search_docs],
                               system_message="Call search_docs to find passages for the user's question. If the "
                                              "question has several parts, call search_docs once per part. Do not "
                                              "answer the question.")
    answerer = AssistantAgent("answerer", model_client=client,
                              system_message="Answer the question using ONLY the retrieved passages. Cite file "
                                             "names. If the passages do not contain the answer, say so.")
    checker = AssistantAgent("checker", model_client=client,
                             system_message="Verify every claim in the answer against the passages. If all are "
                                            "supported, reply 'VERIFIED: <the answer>'. Otherwise list the "
                                            "unsupported claims.")
    team = RoundRobinGroupChat([retriever, answerer, checker], termination_condition=(
        TextMentionTermination("VERIFIED", sources=["checker"]) | MaxMessageTermination(7)))
    await Console(team.run_stream(task=question))
    await client.close()


def main() -> None:
    question = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]).strip()
    if not question:
        print("Please provide a question about the documents.")
        sys.exit(1)
    asyncio.run(run(question))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Agent 37 - Nested Chats (AutoGen)
docs.text: Framework: AutoGen  ·  Industry: Agent Patterns  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: A writer agent writes a short marketing text, sends the draft to a review panel, and then writes the final version. The review panel is itself a conversation between two agents (a critic and a fact checker). That whole inner chat is used as ONE tool by the writer.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Nested chats with TeamTool: TeamTool(team=review_team, ...) wraps a complete team so another agent can call it like a function. The inner team runs its own conversation and returns its last message.
  • Encapsulation: the writer doesn't know the panel has two members; you could swap the panel for a bigger team without changing the writer.
  • Tool arguments for small models: the first version passed the user's request to review_draft instead of a draft. The tool description and prompt now say exactly what must go in the task argument.

docs.title: The structure
docs.text: writer --calls--> review_draft tool == [critic <-> fact_checker] (inner chat) --feedback--> writer --> FINAL

import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from autogen_agentchat.agents import AssistantAgent
from autogen_agentchat.conditions import MaxMessageTermination, TextMentionTermination
from autogen_agentchat.teams import RoundRobinGroupChat
from autogen_agentchat.tools import TeamTool
from autogen_agentchat.ui import Console

from common.autogen_client import ollama_client
from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL


async def run(task: str) -> None:
    client = ollama_client(DEFAULT_MODEL)

    # Inner chat: two reviewers talk to each other about a draft
    critic = AssistantAgent("critic", model_client=client,
                            system_message="Critique the draft for clarity and persuasiveness. Give 3 bullet points.")
    fact_checker = AssistantAgent("fact_checker", model_client=client,
                                  system_message="Point out any claims that are vague, exaggerated or unverifiable. "
                                                 "Then summarise all feedback in 3 bullets and end with DONE.")
    review_team = RoundRobinGroupChat([critic, fact_checker], termination_condition=(
        TextMentionTermination("DONE", sources=["fact_checker"]) | MaxMessageTermination(3)))

    # The whole inner chat is exposed as ONE tool of the outer agent: a nested chat
    review_tool = TeamTool(team=review_team, name="review_draft",
                           description="Send a COMPLETE written draft to the review panel and get their combined "
                                       "feedback. The task argument must contain the full draft text.",
                           return_value_as_last_message=True)

    writer = AssistantAgent(
        "writer", model_client=client, tools=[review_tool], max_tool_iterations=2, reflect_on_tool_use=True,
        system_message="You write short marketing texts, and every text must be reviewed. Your FIRST action is "
                       "always a call to review_draft; do not write any message before it. Compose the draft in "
                       "your head and pass it as task = 'Review this draft: <your full draft>' (never the user's "
                       "request). After you get the feedback, apply it and output only the improved text after "
                       "the heading 'FINAL:'.")
    await Console(writer.run_stream(task=task))
    await client.close()


def main() -> None:
    task = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]).strip()
    if not task:
        print('Please provide a task, e.g. main.py "Write an 80-word product description for a smart water bottle"')
        sys.exit(1)
    asyncio.run(run(task))

import argparse
import asyncio
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from autogen_agentchat.agents import AssistantAgent, SocietyOfMindAgent
from autogen_agentchat.conditions import MaxMessageTermination, TextMentionTermination
from autogen_agentchat.teams import RoundRobinGroupChat
from autogen_agentchat.ui import Console

from common.autogen_client import ollama_client
from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL


async def run(task: str, language: str) -> None:
    client = ollama_client(DEFAULT_MODEL, temperature=0.3)

    # The "inner mind": a writer and an editor discuss until the editor approves
    writer = AssistantAgent("writer", model_client=client,
                            system_message="Write or revise the text. Keep it under 120 words.")
    editor = AssistantAgent("editor", model_client=client,
                            system_message="Give the writer 2 concrete improvements. When the latest draft is good, "
                                           "reply only APPROVE.")
    inner = RoundRobinGroupChat([writer, editor], termination_condition=(
        TextMentionTermination("APPROVE", sources=["editor"]) | MaxMessageTermination(5)))

    # From outside, the whole inner team looks like ONE agent that answers with a single final message
    society = SocietyOfMindAgent("author", team=inner, model_client=client,
                                 response_prompt="Output only the final approved text, with no commentary.")
    translator = AssistantAgent("translator", model_client=client,
                                system_message=f"Translate the author's text into {language}. Output only the "
                                               "translation.")
    outer = RoundRobinGroupChat([society, translator], termination_condition=MaxMessageTermination(3))
    await Console(outer.run_stream(task=task))
    await client.close()


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="AutoGen Society of Mind: an inner team acting as one agent")
    p.add_argument("task", nargs="?", default="")
    p.add_argument("--language", default="Spanish")
    a = p.parse_args()
    if not a.task.strip():
        print('Please provide a task, e.g. main.py "Write a welcome message for new gym members" --language French')
        sys.exit(1)
    asyncio.run(run(a.task.strip(), a.language))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Agent 48 - Conversational Chess (AutoGen)
docs.text: Framework: AutoGen  ·  Industry: Gaming  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Two LLM agents play chess for a set number of half-moves, with a line of friendly trash talk per move. The board is printed after every move and the final position is shown in FEN.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• The environment owns the state; agents only propose: the code holds the chess.Board, shows each player the board and the list of legal moves, and validates every proposed move with python-chess. Illegal moves are sent back with the legal list (up to 3 tries); after that the referee plays a random legal move and says so.
  • Structured agent output in AutoGen: AssistantAgent(output_content_type=Move) makes each reply a Move{move, trash_talk} object instead of free text.
  • Short memory: BufferedChatCompletionContext(buffer_size=6) keeps only the last few turns in each agent's context, so long games don't overflow it.
  • Why not a tool-calling group chat? The first two versions let the players call get_legal_moves/make_move tools inside a RoundRobinGroupChat. With a 7B model they either guessed illegal moves (in UCI notation like g1e4, or moved the opponent's pieces), or skipped the tools and just typed moves as chat text, so the board never changed. Moving control of the game into code made it reliable. Standard notation (e4, Nf3) is used because LLMs know it from chess books.

docs.title: The loop
docs.text: for each half-move: board + legal moves -> player agent -> Move{move, trash_talk} -> code validates -> push or retry

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• LLMs play chess badly: legal, but rarely good moves (in a test both sides mostly shuffled knights).
  • The 7B model often leaves trash_talk empty; the move is what matters to the code.
  • A long game takes a while; keep --moves small.
