import argparse
import asyncio
import random
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

import chess
from autogen_agentchat.agents import AssistantAgent
from autogen_core.model_context import BufferedChatCompletionContext
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from common.autogen_client import ollama_client
from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL

MAX_RETRIES = 3


class Move(BaseModel):
    move: str = Field(description="One move copied exactly from the legal moves list, e.g. e4 or Nf3")
    trash_talk: str = Field(description="One short, friendly sentence to your opponent")


def player(name: str, colour: str, client) -> AssistantAgent:
    return AssistantAgent(
        name, model_client=client,
        output_content_type=Move,  # the agent must answer with a Move object, not free text
        model_context=BufferedChatCompletionContext(buffer_size=6),  # remember only the last few turns
        system_message=f"You play {colour} in a chess game. Each turn you get the board and the list of legal "
                       "moves. Pick a good move and copy it EXACTLY from the list.")


async def choose_move(agent: AssistantAgent, board: chess.Board) -> tuple[chess.Move, str, bool]:
    """Ask the agent for a move; code validates it. Returns (move, trash talk, used_fallback)."""
    legal = ", ".join(board.san(m) for m in board.legal_moves)
    prompt = f"Board (uppercase = White):\n{board}\nLegal moves: {legal}\nYour move?"
    for _ in range(MAX_RETRIES):
        reply = (await agent.run(task=prompt)).messages[-1].content
        try:
            return board.parse_san(reply.move.strip()), reply.trash_talk, False
        except (ValueError, AttributeError):
            bad = getattr(reply, "move", reply)
            print(f"  [referee] {agent.name} tried illegal move {bad!r}, asking again")
            prompt = f"'{bad}' is not legal. Choose EXACTLY one of: {legal}"
    return random.choice(list(board.legal_moves)), "(I'll let the referee pick for me.)", True


async def run(max_moves: int) -> None:
    client = ollama_client(DEFAULT_MODEL, temperature=0.7)
    board = chess.Board()  # the code owns the game state; agents only propose moves
    players = {chess.WHITE: player("white_player", "White", client),
               chess.BLACK: player("black_player", "Black", client)}
    for _ in range(max_moves):
        agent = players[board.turn]
        move, talk, fallback = await choose_move(agent, board)
        san = board.san(move)
        board.push(move)
        note = " (random fallback move)" if fallback else ""
        print(f"\n{agent.name}: {san}{note} - {talk}\n{board}")
        if board.is_game_over():
            print(f"\nGame over: {board.result()} ({board.outcome().termination.name})")
            break
    await client.close()
    print(f"\nFinal position (FEN): {board.fen()}")


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="AutoGen conversational chess between two LLM agents")
    p.add_argument("--moves", type=int, default=10, help="total half-moves to play (2-60)")
    a = p.parse_args()
    if not 2 <= a.moves <= 60:
        print("--moves must be between 2 and 60")
        sys.exit(1)
    asyncio.run(run(a.moves))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import argparse
import asyncio
import csv
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

import yfinance as yf
from autogen_agentchat.agents import AssistantAgent
from autogen_agentchat.conditions import MaxMessageTermination
from autogen_agentchat.teams import RoundRobinGroupChat
from autogen_agentchat.ui import Console

from common.autogen_client import ollama_client
from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL

DEFAULT_PORTFOLIO = Path(__file__).parent / "portfolio.csv"
PORTFOLIO_FILE = DEFAULT_PORTFOLIO


def _closes(ticker: str, period: str = "6mo"):
    return yf.Ticker(ticker).history(period=period)["Close"]


def portfolio_snapshot() -> str:
    """Current value, profit/loss and weight of every holding in the portfolio, plus the total."""
    with open(PORTFOLIO_FILE, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        holdings = list(csv.DictReader(f))
    priced, missing = [], []
    for h in holdings:
        closes = _closes(h["ticker"], "5d")
        if closes.empty:
            missing.append(h["ticker"])
            continue
        shares, cost = float(h["shares"]), float(h["buy_price"])
        price = float(closes.iloc[-1])
        priced.append({"ticker": h["ticker"], "price": price, "value": price * shares,
                       "cost": cost * shares, "pl": (price - cost) * shares})
    total_value = sum(p["value"] for p in priced)
    total_cost = sum(p["cost"] for p in priced)
    lines = [f"{p['ticker']}: price {p['price']:.2f}, value {p['value']:,.2f}, P/L {p['pl']:+,.2f} "
             f"({p['pl'] / p['cost'] * 100:+.1f}%), weight {p['value'] / total_value * 100:.1f}%" for p in priced]
    lines += [f"{t}: no price data" for t in missing]
    return "\n".join(lines) + f"\nTOTAL value {total_value:,.2f}, P/L {total_value - total_cost:+,.2f}"


def technical_indicators(ticker: str) -> str:
    """20/50-day moving averages, 14-day RSI and 1-month price change for one ticker."""
    c = _closes(ticker.upper())
    if len(c) < 50:
        return f"Not enough price history for {ticker}"
    delta = c.diff()
    gain, loss = delta.clip(lower=0).rolling(14).mean(), (-delta.clip(upper=0)).rolling(14).mean()
    rsi = float(100 - 100 / (1 + gain.iloc[-1] / loss.iloc[-1])) if loss.iloc[-1] else 100.0
    sma20, sma50, last = float(c.rolling(20).mean().iloc[-1]), float(c.rolling(50).mean().iloc[-1]), float(c.iloc[-1])
    change = (last / float(c.iloc[-22]) - 1) * 100
    trend = "above" if last > sma50 else "below"
    return (f"{ticker.upper()}: last {last:.2f}, SMA20 {sma20:.2f}, SMA50 {sma50:.2f} (price {trend} SMA50), "
            f"RSI14 {rsi:.0f}, 1-month change {change:+.1f}%")


async def run() -> None:
    client = ollama_client(DEFAULT_MODEL)
    analyst = AssistantAgent(
        "portfolio_analyst", model_client=client, tools=[portfolio_snapshot, technical_indicators],
        max_tool_iterations=8, reflect_on_tool_use=True,
        system_message="Call portfolio_snapshot, then technical_indicators for EVERY ticker in it. Then write: "
                       "a holdings table, total value and P/L, and one line per stock on its trend "
                       "(RSI > 70 = overbought, < 30 = oversold). Use only tool numbers.")
    risk = AssistantAgent(
        "risk_reviewer", model_client=client,
        system_message="Review the analyst's report for risk: concentration (any holding > 35% weight), "
                       "overbought/oversold stocks, and big losers. Give 3 bullet points to watch. "
                       "End with: 'Educational use only, not financial advice.'")
    team = RoundRobinGroupChat([analyst, risk], termination_condition=MaxMessageTermination(3))
    await Console(team.run_stream(task="Review my stock portfolio."))
    await client.close()


def main() -> None:
    global PORTFOLIO_FILE
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="AutoGen stock portfolio watcher")
    p.add_argument("portfolio", nargs="?", default=str(DEFAULT_PORTFOLIO), help="CSV: ticker,shares,buy_price")
    a = p.parse_args()
    PORTFOLIO_FILE = Path(a.portfolio)
    if not PORTFOLIO_FILE.is_file():
        print(f"Portfolio file not found: {PORTFOLIO_FILE}")
        sys.exit(1)
    asyncio.run(run())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.text: Framework: CrewAI  ·  Industry: Travel  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Give it a city, number of days and interests. Three agents work in sequence and print a research list, a day-by-day itinerary and a budget estimate.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• CrewAI model: a crew of role-based agents, each given tasks. You describe who each agent is (role, goal, backstory) instead of drawing a graph.
  • Sequential process: tasks run in order; each task can receive earlier outputs through context=[...].
  • Tools per agent: only the researcher gets web_search. The planner and budgeter just reason over what they are handed.
  • Compare with Agent 01 and 02: one agent with a tool (Agno), an agent in a graph (LangGraph), and now a team with roles (CrewAI).

docs.title: The crew
docs.text:
Researcher (web_search) --> Planner --> Budget Advisor
   8 places + 3 tips      day-by-day     cost table + savings

docs.title: How the code works (main.py)
docs.text:
1. LLM(model="ollama/<model>", base_url=...) points CrewAI at local Ollama through LiteLLM.
  2. @tool("web_search") wraps DuckDuckGo (ddgs) so agents can call it. No API key needed.
  3. Three Agents define roles; three Tasks define the work and expected output.
  4. context=[research] and context=[plan] pass results down the chain.
  5. Crew(..., process=Process.sequential).kickoff() runs it; the script prints each task's output.

import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))
os.environ.setdefault("CREWAI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY", "true")
os.environ.setdefault("OTEL_SDK_DISABLED", "true")

    _s.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")  # Windows console cannot print CrewAI's emoji

from crewai import LLM, Agent, Crew, Process, Task
from crewai.tools import tool
from ddgs import DDGS

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL


@tool("web_search")
def web_search(query: str) -> str:
    """Search the web and return the top results (title, snippet, url)."""
    results = DDGS().text(query, max_results=4)
    return "\n".join(f"- {r['title']}: {r['body']} ({r['href']})" for r in results) or "No results."


def build_crew(city: str, days: int, interests: str) -> Crew:
    llm = LLM(model=f"ollama/{DEFAULT_MODEL}", base_url=OLLAMA_URL, temperature=0.3)

    researcher = Agent(
        role="Local City Researcher",
        goal=f"Find the best sights, food and practical tips in {city}",
        backstory="You know cities well and always check the web for current information.",
        tools=[web_search],
        llm=llm,
        verbose=True,
        allow_delegation=False,
    )
    planner = Agent(
        role="Itinerary Planner",
        goal="Turn research into a realistic day-by-day plan",
        backstory="You group nearby places together and keep each day balanced.",
        llm=llm,
        verbose=True,
        allow_delegation=False,
    )
    budgeter = Agent(
        role="Travel Budget Advisor",
        goal="Estimate costs and give money-saving tips",
        backstory="You give simple, honest daily cost estimates in USD.",
        llm=llm,
        verbose=True,
        allow_delegation=False,
    )

    research = Task(
        description=f"Search the web for {city}. Interests: {interests}. "
        "List 8 attractions or restaurants that match, with one line each, plus 3 practical tips.",
        expected_output="A bullet list of 8 places and 3 tips.",
        agent=researcher,
    )
    plan = Task(
        description=f"Using the research, write a {days}-day itinerary for {city}. "
        "Give morning, afternoon and evening for each day.",
        expected_output=f"A {days}-day itinerary in markdown.",
        agent=planner,
        context=[research],
    )
    budget = Task(
        description=f"Estimate the daily cost in USD (budget, mid-range) for this {days}-day {city} trip "
        "and give 3 ways to save money.",
        expected_output="A short cost table and 3 saving tips.",
        agent=budgeter,
        context=[plan],
    )
    return Crew(agents=[researcher, planner, budgeter], tasks=[research, plan, budget], process=Process.sequential)


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="CrewAI trip planner")
    p.add_argument("city", nargs="?", default="")
    p.add_argument("--days", type=int, default=3)
    p.add_argument("--interests", default="food, history")
    a = p.parse_args()
    if not a.city.strip():
        print("Please provide a city, e.g. main.py Lisbon --days 3")
        sys.exit(1)
    if not 1 <= a.days <= 7:
        print("--days must be between 1 and 7")
        sys.exit(1)
    result = build_crew(a.city.strip(), a.days, a.interests).kickoff()
    for title, out in zip(("RESEARCH", "ITINERARY", "BUDGET"), result.tasks_output):
        print(f"\n===== {title} =====\n")
        print(out.raw)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Framework: CrewAI  ·  Industry: HR  ·  Source folder on GitHub

Guardrails

This agent demonstrates guardrails. Search the code below for GUARDRAIL, and see the Guardrails overview.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Give a company, a role and notes from the hiring manager. A researcher looks up the company on the web, a writer drafts the posting, and a reviewer removes biased wording, trims requirements and keeps it under 400 words. The final posting is printed and saved to output/job_posting.md.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• A writer + reviewer pair: a second agent whose only job is quality control is a cheap way to improve output.
  • Saving task output: Task(output_file=...) makes CrewAI write that task's result to a file automatically.
  • Inclusive-language rules in the backstory: the reviewer checks for gendered words and unrealistic requirement lists.
  • Shared helpers: common/crewai_env.py (telemetry off, UTF-8 console, Ollama LLM) and common/tools.py (web search with fallbacks).

docs.title: Guardrails (CrewAI task guardrails)
docs.text:
Search main.py for GUARDRAIL to find them. Both are attached to the review task: Task(..., guardrails=[posting_rules, FAIRNESS_RULE], guardrail_max_retries=3).

Guardrail Type What it checks posting_rules Python function returning (passed, result_or_feedback) Under 450 words; no biased or gendered words (rockstar, ninja, young, he/his...); has Responsibilities and Requirements sections; no invented salary figures FAIRNESS_RULE plain-English sentence; CrewAI turns it into an LLM check (LLMGuardrail) No requirements based on age, gender, nationality, religion or family status

If a guardrail fails, its feedback goes back to the reviewer agent, which must redo the task (up to 3 times). The [guardrail] lines in the log show each decision. If it still fails after the retries, CrewAI raises an error and the program exits with code 3. Function guardrails are exact and free; LLM guardrails catch meaning that rules can't, but cost a model call and can be wrong.

What testing showed: - A too-broad rule blocks forever. The first salary rule matched any currency amount, so "customer deposits exceeding £25 billion" failed all 4 attempts and the run stopped. The rule now matches only pay (an amount next to "salary/pay" or followed by "per year/hour"). - Feedback must be actionable. "Cut it to under 450 words" produced the same 473-word text on every retry: small models can't count. The feedback now says what to cut (About us to 2 sentences, at most 4 bullets per section, no closing paragraph). In the next run the posting passed first time (425 words). - LLM guardrails are not deterministic. FAIRNESS_RULE rejected a posting saying "Must be under 30 years old / Male candidates preferred" with a clear reason, but once rejected a clean posting too (it passed 3 of 3 retries afterwards). Put hard rules in code and use LLM guardrails for judgement calls.

crewai/09_job_posting_generator/main.py
import argparse
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))
import common.crewai_env  # noqa: F401  (must come before crewai)

from crewai import Agent, Crew, Process, Task, TaskOutput
from crewai.tools import tool

from common.crewai_env import ollama_llm
from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL
from common.tools import web_search as _web_search

OUT = Path(__file__).parent / "output"

# ----- GUARDRAILS ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A CrewAI task guardrail validates the task's output BEFORE it is accepted. Returning (False, feedback) sends
# the feedback to the agent, which must redo the task (up to guardrail_max_retries times).
MAX_WORDS = 450
BIASED_TERMS = ["rockstar", "ninja", "guru", "young", "digital native", "he", "his", "him", "manpower",
                "salesman", "chairman", "native english speaker"]
REQUIRED_SECTIONS = ["Responsibilities", "Requirements"]
# Money that is PAY: an amount next to a pay word, or followed by "per year"/"a year"/"pa". The first version
# flagged ANY currency amount and rejected "customer deposits exceeding £25 billion" on every retry.
SALARY = re.compile(r"(salary|compensation|pay|wage)[^.\n]{0,40}[$£€]\s?\d"
                    r"|[$£€]\s?\d[\d,.]*\s?k?\s*(per (year|annum|hour)|a year|/\s?(year|yr)|p\.?a\b)", re.I)


def posting_rules(result: TaskOutput) -> tuple[bool, Any]:
    """Function guardrail: deterministic checks on the final posting (length, wording, structure, salary)."""
    text = result.raw
    problems = []
    words = len(text.split())
    if words > MAX_WORDS:
        # Small models can't count words, so the feedback says WHAT to cut, not just the number
        problems.append(f"it has {words} words, at least {words - MAX_WORDS + 30} too many: shorten 'About us' "
                        "to 2 sentences, keep at most 4 bullets per section, and delete the closing paragraph")
    found = [t for t in BIASED_TERMS if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(t)}\b", text, re.I)]
    if found:
        problems.append(f"replace biased or gendered wording: {', '.join(found)}")
    missing = [s for s in REQUIRED_SECTIONS if s.lower() not in text.lower()]
    if missing:
        problems.append(f"add the missing sections: {', '.join(missing)}")
    if SALARY.search(text):
        problems.append("remove salary figures; no salary was provided")
    if problems:
        print(f"\n[guardrail] posting rejected -> retry: {'; '.join(problems)}\n")
        return False, "Fix these problems and return the full posting: " + "; ".join(problems)
    print(f"\n[guardrail] posting passed the rules ({words} words)\n")
    return True, result


# A plain-English guardrail: CrewAI turns this sentence into an LLM check (LLMGuardrail) using the agent's model.
FAIRNESS_RULE = ("The job posting must not contain requirements based on age, gender, nationality, religion or "
                 "family status, and must describe the requested role.")
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


@tool("web_search")
def web_search(query: str) -> str:
    """Search the web; returns titles, snippets and URLs."""
    return _web_search(query, 4)


def build_crew(company: str, role: str, notes: str) -> Crew:
    llm = ollama_llm(DEFAULT_MODEL)
    researcher = Agent(role="Company Researcher", goal=f"Understand {company}'s business and culture",
                       backstory="You research companies quickly and summarise what candidates care about.",
                       tools=[web_search], llm=llm, allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)
    writer = Agent(role="Job Description Writer", goal="Write clear, inclusive, attractive job postings",
                   backstory="You are an experienced recruiter who avoids jargon and biased wording.",
                   llm=llm, allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)
    reviewer = Agent(role="Hiring Content Reviewer", goal="Make postings accurate, concise and inclusive",
                     backstory="You check tone, gendered language, unrealistic requirements and length.",
                     llm=llm, allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)

    research = Task(description=f"Search for {company}. Summarise what it does, its products, and its culture "
                                "or values in 5 bullets.",
                    expected_output="5 bullets about the company.", agent=researcher)
    draft = Task(description=f"Write a job posting for a {role} at {company}. Notes from the hiring manager: "
                             f"{notes}. Sections: About us, The role, Responsibilities, Requirements, "
                             "Nice to have, Benefits.",
                 expected_output="A job posting in markdown.", agent=writer, context=[research])
    review = Task(description="Review and improve the posting: remove biased or gendered words, keep requirements "
                              "realistic (max 6), keep it under 400 words. Return the final posting only.",
                  expected_output="The final job posting in markdown.", agent=reviewer, context=[draft],
                  guardrails=[posting_rules, FAIRNESS_RULE],  # GUARDRAILS: code check, then LLM check
                  guardrail_max_retries=3,
                  output_file=str(OUT / "job_posting.md"))  # CrewAI writes the task result to this file
    return Crew(agents=[researcher, writer, reviewer], tasks=[research, draft, review], process=Process.sequential)


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="CrewAI job posting generator")
    p.add_argument("company", nargs="?", default="")
    p.add_argument("--role", default="Junior Python Developer")
    p.add_argument("--notes", default="hybrid work, team of 6, Python and SQL")
    a = p.parse_args()
    if not a.company.strip():
        print('Please provide a company, e.g. main.py "Spotify" --role "Data Analyst"')
        sys.exit(1)
    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    try:
        result = build_crew(a.company.strip(), a.role, a.notes).kickoff()
    except Exception as e:  # raised when the output still fails a guardrail after all retries
        print(f"\n[guardrail] The posting could not pass the guardrails: {e}")
        sys.exit(3)
    print(f"\n===== JOB POSTING (saved to {OUT / 'job_posting.md'}) =====\n{result.raw}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))
import common.crewai_env  # noqa: F401  (must come before crewai)

import yfinance as yf
from crewai import Agent, Crew, Process, Task
from crewai.tools import tool

from common.crewai_env import ollama_llm
from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL
from common.tools import web_search as _web_search


@tool("stock_fundamentals")
def stock_fundamentals(ticker: str) -> str:
    """Get price, valuation and growth figures for a stock ticker such as AAPL."""
    info = yf.Ticker(ticker.strip().upper()).info
    keys = ["longName", "currentPrice", "marketCap", "trailingPE", "forwardPE", "revenueGrowth", "profitMargins",
            "debtToEquity", "fiftyTwoWeekHigh", "fiftyTwoWeekLow", "recommendationKey"]
    return "\n".join(f"{k}: {info.get(k)}" for k in keys) if info.get("longName") else f"No data for {ticker}"


@tool("price_history")
def price_history(ticker: str) -> str:
    """Get monthly closing prices for the last 6 months for a ticker."""
    h = yf.Ticker(ticker.strip().upper()).history(period="6mo", interval="1mo")
    return "\n".join(f"{d.date()}: {c:.2f}" for d, c in h["Close"].items()) or f"No history for {ticker}"


@tool("web_search")
def web_search(query: str) -> str:
    """Search the web for recent news; returns titles, snippets and URLs."""
    return _web_search(query, 5)


def build_crew(ticker: str) -> Crew:
    llm = ollama_llm(DEFAULT_MODEL, temperature=0.2)
    analyst = Agent(role="Financial Data Analyst", goal=f"Explain {ticker}'s numbers accurately",
                    backstory="You only use numbers returned by your tools and never invent figures.",
                    tools=[stock_fundamentals, price_history], llm=llm, allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)
    news = Agent(role="Market News Researcher", goal=f"Find the most important recent news about {ticker}",
                 backstory="You separate facts from rumours and always give sources.",
                 tools=[web_search], llm=llm, allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)
    advisor = Agent(role="Investment Report Writer", goal="Write a balanced, plain-English stock report",
                    backstory="You present bull and bear cases fairly and never give personal advice.",
                    llm=llm, allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)

    t_numbers = Task(description=f"Use stock_fundamentals and price_history for {ticker}. Report valuation, "
                                 "growth, profitability and the 6-month trend.",
                     expected_output="A short table of key figures and 3 observations.", agent=analyst)
    t_news = Task(description=f"Search for news about {ticker} from the last few months. List the 4 most "
                              "important items with one line each and the URL.",
                  expected_output="4 news bullets with URLs.", agent=news)
    t_report = Task(description=f"Write a report on {ticker}: Summary, Key figures, Recent news, Bull case, "
                                "Bear case, Overall view (positive / neutral / negative with one reason). "
                                "End with 'Educational use only, not financial advice.'",
                    expected_output="A markdown report under 450 words.", agent=advisor,
                    context=[t_numbers, t_news])
    return Crew(agents=[analyst, news, advisor], tasks=[t_numbers, t_news, t_report], process=Process.sequential)


def main() -> None:
    ticker = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]).strip().upper()
    if not ticker or not ticker.replace(".", "").replace("-", "").isalnum() or len(ticker) > 10:
        print("Please provide a stock ticker, e.g. main.py NVDA")
        sys.exit(1)
    print(build_crew(ticker).kickoff().raw)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))
import common.crewai_env  # noqa: F401  (must come before crewai)

from crewai import Agent, Crew, Process, Task
from crewai.tools import tool
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from common.crewai_env import ollama_llm
from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL
from common.tools import web_search as _web_search


@tool("web_search")
def web_search(query: str) -> str:
    """Search the web; returns titles, snippets and URLs."""
    return _web_search(query, 4)


class Channel(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(description="e.g. Instagram, SEO blog, email, local events")
    why: str
    first_action: str


class MarketingStrategy(BaseModel):
    target_audience: str
    positioning: str = Field(description="One sentence: why choose us over alternatives")
    key_messages: list[str] = Field(description="3 short messages")
    channels: list[Channel] = Field(description="3 channels")
    kpis: list[str] = Field(description="3 measurable KPIs with targets")


def build_crew(product: str, budget: str) -> Crew:
    llm = ollama_llm(DEFAULT_MODEL)
    researcher = Agent(role="Market Researcher", goal=f"Understand the market and competitors for {product}",
                       backstory="You find who buys this kind of product and what competitors do well.",
                       tools=[web_search], llm=llm, allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)
    strategist = Agent(role="Marketing Strategist", goal="Turn research into a focused, realistic plan",
                       backstory="You work with small budgets and prefer few channels done well.",
                       llm=llm, allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)

    research = Task(description=f"Research the market for: {product}. Find 3 competitors or alternatives, "
                                "the typical customer, and 3 trends. Use web_search.",
                    expected_output="Bullets: competitors, typical customer, trends.", agent=researcher)
    strategy = Task(description=f"Create a marketing strategy for {product} with a monthly budget of {budget}.",
                    expected_output="A marketing strategy.", agent=strategist, context=[research],
                    output_pydantic=MarketingStrategy)  # the result is validated into this Pydantic model
    return Crew(agents=[researcher, strategist], tasks=[research, strategy], process=Process.sequential)


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="CrewAI marketing strategy with structured output")
    p.add_argument("product", nargs="?", default="")
    p.add_argument("--budget", default="1000 USD")
    a = p.parse_args()
    if not a.product.strip():
        print('Please describe the product, e.g. main.py "a vegan bakery in Manchester"')
        sys.exit(1)
    result = build_crew(a.product.strip(), a.budget).kickoff()
    s: MarketingStrategy | None = result.pydantic
    if s is None:
        print(result.raw)
        return
    print(f"\n===== STRATEGY: {a.product} =====\nAudience: {s.target_audience}\nPositioning: {s.positioning}\n")
    print("Key messages:\n" + "\n".join(f"- {m}" for m in s.key_messages))
    print("\nChannels:")
    for c in s.channels:
        print(f"- {c.name}: {c.why}\n    first action: {c.first_action}")
    print("\nKPIs:\n" + "\n".join(f"- {k}" for k in s.kpis))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Screens the CVs in data/candidates/ against data/job_description.txt. Each must-have is checked against the CV with quoted evidence, a score is computed, then an interviewer writes targeted questions and HR writes a shortlist. All candidates are fictional.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• One document per task: a screening task is created per CV, which is more reliable for small models than one prompt with every CV.
  • Evidence-based checks: each requirement must cite "exact words from the CV" or say "not in CV", which reduces invented skills.
  • The model judges, code scores: in the first version the model gave a score directly and rated a candidate missing 2 of 4 must-haves at 85/100. Now score is a Python property: the share of must-haves met. Numbers that matter should be computed, not generated.
  • Two crews in sequence: a screening crew, then a reporting crew that receives the computed ranking.

CV 1..N -> [CV Screener -> CandidateScore] -> code computes scores and ranks
        -> Interview Designer -> HR Coordinator -> shortlist

import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))
import common.crewai_env  # noqa: F401  (must come before crewai)

from crewai import Agent, Crew, Process, Task
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from common.crewai_env import ollama_llm
from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL

DATA = Path(__file__).parent / "data"


class Requirement(BaseModel):
    requirement: str = Field(description="One must-have from the job description, e.g. 'SQL'")
    met: bool
    evidence: str = Field(description="Exact words from the CV that prove it, or 'not in CV'")


class CandidateScore(BaseModel):
    name: str
    must_haves: list[Requirement] = Field(description="One entry for EVERY must-have in the job description")
    summary: str = Field(description="Two sentences")

    @property
    def score(self) -> int:
        """Computed in code, not by the model: the share of must-haves that are met."""
        return round(100 * sum(r.met for r in self.must_haves) / max(len(self.must_haves), 1))

    @property
    def missing(self) -> list[str]:
        return [r.requirement for r in self.must_haves if not r.met]


def build_crew(job: str, cvs: dict[str, str]) -> tuple[Crew, list[Task], Agent, Agent]:
    llm = ollama_llm(DEFAULT_MODEL, temperature=0)
    screener = Agent(role="CV Screener", goal="Score each candidate fairly against the must-have requirements",
                     backstory="You only use facts written in the CV and ignore names, gender and age.",
                     llm=llm, allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)
    interviewer = Agent(role="Interview Designer", goal="Prepare targeted interview questions",
                        backstory="You probe gaps and verify claimed skills with practical questions.",
                        llm=llm, allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)
    hr = Agent(role="HR Coordinator", goal="Give the hiring manager a clear shortlist",
               backstory="You write short, decision-ready summaries.", llm=llm, allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)

    # One screening task per CV: small models are more reliable with one document at a time
    screens = [Task(description=f"Job description:\n{job}\n\nCV:\n{cv}\n\nFor EACH must-have in the job "
                                "description, decide if the CV shows it and quote the evidence. A skill only "
                                "counts if the CV states it.",
                    expected_output="A requirement-by-requirement check.", agent=screener,
                    output_pydantic=CandidateScore)
               for cv in cvs.values()]
    return Crew(agents=[screener], tasks=screens, process=Process.sequential), screens, interviewer, hr


def report_crew(ranking: str, interviewer: Agent, hr: Agent) -> Crew:
    questions = Task(description=f"Screening results (scores computed from must-haves met):\n{ranking}\n\n"
                                 "Write 3 interview questions for each of the top 2 candidates that probe their "
                                 "missing or unproven skills.",
                     expected_output="Questions grouped by candidate.", agent=interviewer)
    shortlist = Task(description=f"Screening results:\n{ranking}\n\nWrite the hiring manager a shortlist in the "
                                 "same order (do not change scores), a recommendation of who to interview, and the "
                                 "questions.",
                     expected_output="A markdown shortlist.", agent=hr, context=[questions])
    return Crew(agents=[interviewer, hr], tasks=[questions, shortlist], process=Process.sequential)


def main() -> None:
    job_file, cv_dir = DATA / "job_description.txt", DATA / "candidates"
    cvs = {p.stem: p.read_text(encoding="utf-8") for p in sorted(cv_dir.glob("*.txt"))}
    if not job_file.exists() or not cvs:
        print(f"Need {job_file} and at least one CV in {cv_dir}")
        sys.exit(1)
    screen_crew, screens, interviewer, hr = build_crew(job_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), cvs)
    screen_crew.kickoff()
    scored = sorted((t.output.pydantic for t in screens if t.output and t.output.pydantic), key=lambda s: -s.score)
    ranking = "\n".join(f"{s.score:>3}  {s.name}: missing {s.missing or 'nothing'} - {s.summary}" for s in scored)
    print(f"\n===== SCORES (computed in code) =====\n{ranking}")
    for s in scored:
        for r in s.must_haves:
            print(f"   {s.name:<14} {'MET ' if r.met else 'MISS'} {r.requirement}: {r.evidence}")
    result = report_crew(ranking, interviewer, hr).kickoff()
    print(f"\n===== SHORTLIST =====\n{result.raw}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))
import common.crewai_env  # noqa: F401  (must come before crewai)

from crewai import Agent, Crew, Process, Task
from crewai.tools import tool

from common.crewai_env import ollama_llm
from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL
from common.tools import web_search as _web_search


@tool("web_search")
def web_search(query: str) -> str:
    """Search the web; returns titles, snippets and URLs."""
    return _web_search(query, 4)


def build_crew(company: str, objective: str, attendees: str) -> Crew:
    llm = ollama_llm(DEFAULT_MODEL)
    researcher = Agent(role="Company Researcher", goal=f"Brief the team on {company}",
                       backstory="You find recent, relevant facts and cite sources.",
                       tools=[web_search], llm=llm, allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)
    industry = Agent(role="Industry Analyst", goal=f"Explain the industry context around {company}",
                     backstory="You spot trends, competitors and pressures that matter in a meeting.",
                     tools=[web_search], llm=llm, allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)
    strategist = Agent(role="Meeting Strategist", goal="Prepare talking points and smart questions",
                       backstory="You turn research into a plan that helps reach the meeting objective.",
                       llm=llm, allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)
    writer = Agent(role="Briefing Writer", goal="Produce a one-page briefing",
                   backstory="You write tight, skimmable briefings for busy people.",
                   llm=llm, allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)

    t1 = Task(description=f"Research {company}: what it does, size, recent news (last 6 months), and anything "
                          f"about these attendees: {attendees}. Use web_search. Cite URLs.",
              expected_output="Bullets with sources.", agent=researcher)
    t2 = Task(description=f"Describe {company}'s industry: 3 trends, 3 competitors, 2 challenges.",
              expected_output="Short bullets.", agent=industry)
    t3 = Task(description=f"Meeting objective: {objective}. Write 4 talking points, 5 questions to ask, and 3 "
                          "likely objections with answers.",
              expected_output="Talking points, questions and objections.", agent=strategist, context=[t1, t2])
    t4 = Task(description="Combine everything into a one-page briefing: Objective, Company snapshot, Attendees, "
                          "Industry context, Talking points, Questions, Objections, Sources.",
              expected_output="A markdown briefing under 500 words.", agent=writer, context=[t1, t2, t3])
    return Crew(agents=[researcher, industry, strategist, writer], tasks=[t1, t2, t3, t4],
                process=Process.sequential)


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="CrewAI meeting preparation")
    p.add_argument("company", nargs="?", default="")
    p.add_argument("--objective", default="explore a partnership")
    p.add_argument("--attendees", default="unknown")
    a = p.parse_args()
    if not a.company.strip():
        print('Please provide a company, e.g. main.py "Duolingo" --objective "sell our analytics tool"')
        sys.exit(1)
    print(build_crew(a.company.strip(), a.objective, a.attendees).kickoff().raw)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import argparse
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))
import common.crewai_env  # noqa: F401  (must come before crewai)

from crewai import Agent, Crew, Process, Task

from common.crewai_env import ollama_llm
from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL

OUT = Path(__file__).parent / "output"


def build_crew(idea: str) -> Crew:
    analyst = Agent(role="Product Analyst", goal="Clarify the idea's audience, problem and value",
                    backstory="You turn a vague idea into a crisp value proposition.",
                    llm=ollama_llm(DEFAULT_MODEL), allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)
    copywriter = Agent(role="Conversion Copywriter", goal="Write landing-page copy that converts",
                       backstory="You write short headlines, benefit-led sections and clear calls to action.",
                       llm=ollama_llm(DEFAULT_MODEL, temperature=0.5), allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)
    developer = Agent(role="Front-end Developer", goal="Build a clean, responsive single-file landing page",
                      backstory="You write semantic HTML with inline CSS, no external libraries.",
                      llm=ollama_llm(DEFAULT_MODEL, temperature=0.1), allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)

    t1 = Task(description=f"Idea: {idea}. Define: target audience, main problem, 3 key benefits, one-line "
                          "value proposition.", expected_output="Short bullets.", agent=analyst)
    t2 = Task(description="Write the landing-page copy: hero headline + subheadline, 3 benefit sections "
                          "(title + 2 sentences), 3 FAQs, and a call-to-action button text.",
              expected_output="Copy organised by section.", agent=copywriter, context=[t1])
    t3 = Task(description="Build ONE complete HTML5 file using the copy. Inline <style> only, mobile-friendly, "
                          "a hero section, benefit cards, FAQ, footer. Output only the HTML, starting with "
                          "<!DOCTYPE html>.",
              expected_output="A complete HTML document.", agent=developer, context=[t2])
    return Crew(agents=[analyst, copywriter, developer], tasks=[t1, t2, t3], process=Process.sequential)


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="CrewAI landing page generator")
    p.add_argument("idea", nargs="?", default="")
    a = p.parse_args()
    if not a.idea.strip():
        print('Please describe the idea, e.g. main.py "an app that reminds you to water your plants"')
        sys.exit(1)
    raw = build_crew(a.idea.strip()).kickoff().raw
    match = re.search(r"<!DOCTYPE html>.*</html>", raw, re.S | re.I)  # strip any text around the HTML
    if not match:
        print("The developer did not return a full HTML page. Raw output:\n" + raw)
        sys.exit(2)
    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    page = OUT / "index.html"
    page.write_text(match.group(0), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"\nSaved {page} ({len(match.group(0))} characters). Open it in a browser.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))
import common.crewai_env  # noqa: F401  (must come before crewai)

from crewai import Agent, Crew, Process, Task

from common.crewai_env import ollama_llm
from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL

DEFAULT_STORY = Path(__file__).parent / "story.txt"


def build_crew(text: str) -> Crew:
    llm = ollama_llm(DEFAULT_MODEL, temperature=0.4)
    cleaner = Agent(role="Content Cleaner", goal="Remove spam, ads and off-topic lines",
                    backstory="You keep every real line of the conversation and drop the noise.",
                    llm=ollama_llm(DEFAULT_MODEL, temperature=0), allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)
    analyst = Agent(role="Story Analyst", goal="Find the characters, conflict and story beats",
                    backstory="You are a script editor who sees the drama in everyday conversations.",
                    llm=llm, allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)
    writer = Agent(role="Screenwriter", goal="Write a short, funny scene in proper screenplay format",
                   backstory="You write tight comedy with action lines and natural dialogue.",
                   llm=ollama_llm(DEFAULT_MODEL, temperature=0.7), allow_delegation=False, verbose=True)

    t1 = Task(description=f"Remove any spam or advertising from this text and return the rest unchanged:\n{text}",
              expected_output="The cleaned text.", agent=cleaner)
    t2 = Task(description="List the characters (one line each), the central conflict, and 4 story beats.",
              expected_output="Characters, conflict, beats.", agent=analyst, context=[t1])
    t3 = Task(description="Write a one-scene screenplay (about 300 words) in standard format: scene heading "
                          "(INT. OFFICE KITCHEN - MORNING), action lines, CHARACTER NAMES in caps above dialogue. "
                          "Keep the real events; add physical comedy.",
              expected_output="A screenplay scene.", agent=writer, context=[t1, t2])
    return Crew(agents=[cleaner, analyst, writer], tasks=[t1, t2, t3], process=Process.sequential)


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="CrewAI screenplay writer: turns a conversation into a scene")
    p.add_argument("file", nargs="?", default=str(DEFAULT_STORY))
    a = p.parse_args()
    path = Path(a.file)
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip() if path.is_file() else ""
    if not text:
        print(f"File not found or empty: {path}")
        sys.exit(1)
    print("\n===== SCREENPLAY =====\n" + build_crew(text).kickoff().raw)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Deterministic tool + LLM explanation: the lint() function finds problems with plain rules (heading spacing and level jumps, duplicate headings, mixed list markers, unclosed links, code blocks without a language, trailing spaces, long lines).   • Single-agent crew: a crew can have just one agent and one task; you still get CrewAI's tool handling and logging.
  • Testing the tool alone: lint() is plain Python, so you can test it without any model (see "Things to try").

docs.title: Agent 02 - Agentic RAG (LangGraph)
docs.text: Framework: LangGraph  ·  Industry: Knowledge & RAG  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Answers questions about a company handbook (docs/acme_handbook.md). The agent decides whether it needs to search the handbook. Greetings get a direct reply; policy questions trigger a search first.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• RAG (retrieval-augmented generation): instead of trusting the model's memory, fetch relevant text from your own documents and answer from that.
  • "Agentic" RAG: retrieval is a tool the model chooses to call, not a fixed step. Classic RAG always retrieves; agentic RAG retrieves only when useful, and can search again if the first result is not enough.
  • LangGraph basics: a graph of nodes (functions) joined by edges, sharing a state. Here the state is just the message list.
  • Embeddings: each handbook section is turned into a vector; a question is turned into a vector too, and the closest sections are returned.

docs.title: The graph
docs.text:
START -> agent --(tool requested?)--> tools -> agent -> ... -> END
                 \--(no)--> END
- agent node: the model, with the search tool attached. - tools node: runs search_handbook when the model asks. - tools_condition: the router. Tool call in the reply goes to tools; otherwise the run ends. - The tools -> agent edge is the loop: the model reads the results and can answer or search again.

docs.title: How the code works (main.py)
docs.text:
1. MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter cuts the handbook into one chunk per ## section.
  2. OllamaEmbeddings + InMemoryVectorStore embed and store the chunks (rebuilt at every start; fine for a small file).
  3. search_handbook is a @tool returning the top 2 chunks with their section names.
  4. The system prompt tells the model when to search, to answer only from results, and to cite the section.
  5. stream prints each tool call, then the final answer.

  • Ask about something not in the handbook (pets) and check it admits it does not know.
  • Change k=2 to k=1 or k=4 in search_handbook and see how answers change.
  • Ask a question spanning two sections ("remote work and equipment") and see if it searches twice.

docs.title: Known limits

• No relevance check on retrieved text. Agent 13 (Corrective RAG) adds that.
  • Index is rebuilt on every run and held in memory only.
  • Needs a model with good tool calling (qwen2.5:7b-instruct works).

langgraph/02_agentic_rag/main.py
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from langchain_core.documents import Document
from langchain_core.tools import tool
from langchain_core.vectorstores import InMemoryVectorStore
from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama, OllamaEmbeddings
from langchain_text_splitters import MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter
from langgraph.graph import END, START, MessagesState, StateGraph
from langgraph.prebuilt import ToolNode, tools_condition

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, EMBED_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL

DOCS_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "docs"
SYSTEM = (
    "You answer questions about the company handbook. "
    "For any question about company policy, call search_handbook first, "
    "then answer only from what it returns and name the section you used. "
    "If the handbook does not cover it, say so. For greetings, answer directly without searching."
)


def build_store() -> InMemoryVectorStore:
    splitter = MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter([("#", "title"), ("##", "section")])
    chunks: list[Document] = []
    for path in sorted(DOCS_DIR.glob("*.md")):
        chunks += splitter.split_text(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    store = InMemoryVectorStore(OllamaEmbeddings(model=EMBED_MODEL, base_url=OLLAMA_URL))
    store.add_documents(chunks)
    return store


def build_graph():
    store = build_store()

    @tool
    def search_handbook(query: str) -> str:
        """Search the company handbook for policy information."""
        hits = store.similarity_search(query, k=2)
        return "\n\n".join(f"[{d.metadata.get('section', '?')}] {d.page_content}" for d in hits)

    llm = ChatOllama(model=DEFAULT_MODEL, base_url=OLLAMA_URL, temperature=0).bind_tools([search_handbook])

    def agent(state: MessagesState):
        return {"messages": [llm.invoke([("system", SYSTEM)] + state["messages"])]}

    g = StateGraph(MessagesState)
    g.add_node("agent", agent)
    g.add_node("tools", ToolNode([search_handbook]))
    g.add_edge(START, "agent")
    g.add_conditional_edges("agent", tools_condition)
    g.add_edge("tools", "agent")
    return g.compile()


def main() -> None:
    question = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]).strip()
    if not question:
        print("Please provide a question.")
        sys.exit(1)
    for step in build_graph().stream({"messages": [("user", question)]}, stream_mode="values"):
        msg = step["messages"][-1]
        for call in getattr(msg, "tool_calls", None) or []:
            print(f"[tool call] {call['name']}({call['args']})")
        if msg.type == "ai" and msg.content:
            final = msg.content
    print("\n" + final)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Agent 08 - Reflection Agent (LangGraph)
docs.text: Framework: LangGraph  ·  Industry: Agent Patterns  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Give it a writing task. It writes a draft, a strict "editor" critiques it with 3 concrete improvements, and the writer rewrites. This repeats for --rounds drafts; every draft and critique is printed.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Reflection pattern: the same model plays two roles (writer and critic) with different prompts. Self-critique often improves output without any tools.
  • Custom state: instead of a message list, the state is a TypedDict with task, draft, critique, round, max_rounds.
  • Loops in a graph: generate -> reflect -> generate is a cycle; the conditional edge should_continue stops it after max_rounds.

docs.title: The graph
docs.text:
START -> generate --(round < max)--> reflect -> generate -> ... 
                  \--(done)--> END

  • Change the critic's focus (for example "make it funnier" or "cut 30% of the words").
  • Use a different model as the critic.

• Critiques can push the writer to invent specifics (in a test it added "web development" that the task never mentioned).
  • More rounds is not always better; drafts can get longer and blander.

langgraph/08_reflection_agent/main.py
import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TypedDict

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama
from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL


class State(TypedDict):
    task: str
    draft: str
    critique: str
    round: int
    max_rounds: int


llm = ChatOllama(model=DEFAULT_MODEL, base_url=OLLAMA_URL, temperature=0.4)


def generate(state: State) -> dict:
    if state["critique"]:
        prompt = (f"Task: {state['task']}\n\nYour previous draft:\n{state['draft']}\n\n"
                  f"Reviewer feedback:\n{state['critique']}\n\nRewrite the draft applying every point. "
                  "Output only the new draft.")
    else:
        prompt = f"Task: {state['task']}\nWrite the best possible response. Output only the draft."
    draft = llm.invoke(prompt).content
    print(f"\n----- DRAFT {state['round'] + 1} -----\n{draft}")
    return {"draft": draft, "round": state["round"] + 1}


def reflect(state: State) -> dict:
    prompt = (f"You are a strict editor. Task: {state['task']}\n\nDraft:\n{state['draft']}\n\n"
              "Give 3 specific, actionable improvements as a numbered list (clarity, accuracy, structure, tone). "
              "Do not rewrite the draft.")
    critique = llm.invoke(prompt).content
    print(f"\n----- CRITIQUE {state['round']} -----\n{critique}")
    return {"critique": critique}


def should_continue(state: State) -> str:
    return "reflect" if state["round"] < state["max_rounds"] else END


def build_graph():
    g = StateGraph(State)
    g.add_node("generate", generate)
    g.add_node("reflect", reflect)
    g.add_edge(START, "generate")
    g.add_conditional_edges("generate", should_continue, ["reflect", END])
    g.add_edge("reflect", "generate")
    return g.compile()


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="LangGraph reflection agent: draft, critique, rewrite")
    p.add_argument("task", nargs="?", default="")
    p.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=2, help="number of drafts (1-4)")
    a = p.parse_args()
    if not a.task.strip():
        print('Please provide a writing task, e.g. main.py "Write a LinkedIn post about learning Python"')
        sys.exit(1)
    rounds = max(1, min(a.rounds, 4))
    final = build_graph().invoke({"task": a.task.strip(), "draft": "", "critique": "", "round": 0,
                                  "max_rounds": rounds})
    print(f"\n===== FINAL (after {final['round']} drafts) =====\n{final['draft']}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Agent 13 - Corrective RAG (LangGraph)
docs.text: Framework: LangGraph  ·  Industry: Knowledge & RAG  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Answers questions from the company handbook (docs/acme_handbook.md), but first grades every retrieved chunk for relevance. If nothing relevant is found, it rewrites the question as a web query and searches the web instead. The output says where the answer came from.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• CRAG (Corrective RAG): plain RAG trusts whatever the retriever returns. CRAG adds a grader that throws away irrelevant chunks and a fallback when the knowledge base can't answer. This fixes the "known limit" of Agent 02.
  • LLM as a classifier: llm.with_structured_output(Grade) forces a strict yes/no answer per chunk.
  • Branching: the conditional edge decide chooses between generate and web_search.

docs.title: The graph
docs.text:
START -> retrieve -> grade --(relevant chunks)--> generate -> END
                          \--(none)--> web_search -> generate

  • The fallback replaces the handbook entirely; it does not mix both sources.

import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal, TypedDict

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from ddgs import DDGS
from langchain_core.vectorstores import InMemoryVectorStore
from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama, OllamaEmbeddings
from langchain_text_splitters import MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter
from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph
from pydantic import BaseModel

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, EMBED_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL

DOCS_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "docs"
llm = ChatOllama(model=DEFAULT_MODEL, base_url=OLLAMA_URL, temperature=0)


class Grade(BaseModel):
    relevant: Literal["yes", "no"]


class State(TypedDict):
    question: str
    documents: list[str]
    source: str
    answer: str


def build_store() -> InMemoryVectorStore:
    splitter = MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter([("#", "title"), ("##", "section")])
    chunks = [c for p in DOCS_DIR.glob("*.md") for c in splitter.split_text(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))]
    store = InMemoryVectorStore(OllamaEmbeddings(model=EMBED_MODEL, base_url=OLLAMA_URL))
    store.add_documents(chunks)
    return store


STORE = build_store()


def retrieve(state: State) -> dict:
    docs = STORE.similarity_search(state["question"], k=3)
    print(f"[retrieve] {len(docs)} chunks from the handbook")
    return {"documents": [d.page_content for d in docs], "source": "handbook"}


def grade_documents(state: State) -> dict:
    grader = llm.with_structured_output(Grade)
    kept = []
    for doc in state["documents"]:
        g = grader.invoke(f"Question: {state['question']}\n\nDocument:\n{doc}\n\n"
                          "Does the document contain information that helps answer the question? yes or no.")
        print(f"[grade] {g.relevant}: {doc[:60]!r}")
        if g.relevant == "yes":
            kept.append(doc)
    return {"documents": kept}


def decide(state: State) -> str:
    if state["documents"]:
        return "generate"
    print("[decide] no relevant handbook text -> web search")
    return "web_search"


def web_search(state: State) -> dict:
    query = llm.invoke(f"Rewrite this as a short web search query. Output only the query.\n{state['question']}").content
    print(f"[web_search] {query.strip()}")
    results = DDGS().text(query.strip().strip('"'), max_results=4)
    return {"documents": [f"{r['title']}: {r['body']} ({r['href']})" for r in results], "source": "web"}


def generate(state: State) -> dict:
    context = "\n\n".join(state["documents"])
    answer = llm.invoke(f"Answer the question using only this context. Be concise.\n\nContext:\n{context}\n\n"
                        f"Question: {state['question']}").content
    return {"answer": answer}


def build_graph():
    g = StateGraph(State)
    for name, fn in [("retrieve", retrieve), ("grade", grade_documents), ("web_search", web_search),
                     ("generate", generate)]:
        g.add_node(name, fn)
    g.add_edge(START, "retrieve")
    g.add_edge("retrieve", "grade")
    g.add_conditional_edges("grade", decide, ["generate", "web_search"])
    g.add_edge("web_search", "generate")
    g.add_edge("generate", END)
    return g.compile()


def main() -> None:
    question = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]).strip()
    if not question:
        print("Please provide a question.")
        sys.exit(1)
    out = build_graph().invoke({"question": question, "documents": [], "source": "", "answer": ""})
    print(f"\n[answered from: {out['source']}]\n{out['answer']}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Agent 17 - Self-RAG (LangGraph)
docs.text: Framework: LangGraph  ·  Industry: Knowledge & RAG  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Answers handbook questions and then checks its own answer twice: is every claim supported by the retrieved text (no hallucination), and does it actually answer the question? If not, it regenerates or rewrites the search query and tries again (up to 2 retries).

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Self-RAG: checks happen after generation, not just before. Agent 13 checks the inputs; this agent checks the output.
  • Two kinds of failure, two fixes: not grounded -> regenerate; grounded but not useful -> rewrite the query and retrieve again.
  • Retry limits: a tries counter in state stops endless loops.

docs.title: The graph
docs.text:
START -> retrieve -> grade_documents -> generate --(grounded and useful)--> END
                ^                         |--(not grounded)--> generate
                |                         \--(not useful)--> rewrite_query
                \------------------------------------------------/

  • Set MAX_TRIES = 0 to disable retries.

  • Each check is an extra LLM call (slower than plain RAG).

import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal, TypedDict

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from langchain_core.vectorstores import InMemoryVectorStore
from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama, OllamaEmbeddings
from langchain_text_splitters import MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter
from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph
from pydantic import BaseModel

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, EMBED_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL

DOCS_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "docs"
MAX_TRIES = 2
llm = ChatOllama(model=DEFAULT_MODEL, base_url=OLLAMA_URL, temperature=0)


class YesNo(BaseModel):
    score: Literal["yes", "no"]


class State(TypedDict):
    question: str
    search_query: str
    documents: list[str]
    answer: str
    tries: int


def build_store() -> InMemoryVectorStore:
    splitter = MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter([("#", "title"), ("##", "section")])
    chunks = [c for p in DOCS_DIR.glob("*.md") for c in splitter.split_text(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))]
    store = InMemoryVectorStore(OllamaEmbeddings(model=EMBED_MODEL, base_url=OLLAMA_URL))
    store.add_documents(chunks)
    return store


STORE = build_store()


def ask_yes_no(prompt: str) -> str:
    return llm.with_structured_output(YesNo).invoke(prompt).score


def retrieve(state: State) -> dict:
    docs = STORE.similarity_search(state["search_query"], k=3)
    print(f"[retrieve] query={state['search_query']!r}")
    return {"documents": [d.page_content for d in docs]}


def grade_documents(state: State) -> dict:
    kept = [d for d in state["documents"]
            if ask_yes_no(f"Question: {state['question']}\nDocument: {d}\nIs the document relevant? yes or no.") == "yes"]
    print(f"[grade_documents] kept {len(kept)} of {len(state['documents'])}")
    return {"documents": kept}


def generate(state: State) -> dict:
    context = "\n\n".join(state["documents"]) or "(no relevant documents)"
    answer = llm.invoke(f"Answer using only the context. If it is not there, say you don't know.\n\n"
                        f"Context:\n{context}\n\nQuestion: {state['question']}").content
    print(f"[generate] try {state['tries'] + 1}")
    return {"answer": answer, "tries": state["tries"] + 1}


def check_answer(state: State) -> str:
    """Self-critique: is the answer grounded in the documents, and does it answer the question?"""
    if state["tries"] > MAX_TRIES:
        print("[check] giving up after max tries")
        return "done"
    context = "\n\n".join(state["documents"])
    grounded = ask_yes_no(f"Facts:\n{context}\n\nAnswer: {state['answer']}\n"
                          "Is every claim in the answer supported by the facts? yes or no.")
    print(f"[check] grounded: {grounded}")
    if grounded == "no":
        return "regenerate"
    useful = ask_yes_no(f"Question: {state['question']}\nAnswer: {state['answer']}\n"
                        "Does the answer resolve the question? yes or no.")
    print(f"[check] answers the question: {useful}")
    return "done" if useful == "yes" else "rewrite"


def rewrite_query(state: State) -> dict:
    new = llm.invoke(f"Rewrite this question so it finds better matches in a company handbook. "
                     f"Output only the rewritten question.\n{state['question']}").content.strip()
    return {"search_query": new}


def build_graph():
    g = StateGraph(State)
    g.add_node("retrieve", retrieve)
    g.add_node("grade_documents", grade_documents)
    g.add_node("generate", generate)
    g.add_node("rewrite_query", rewrite_query)
    g.add_edge(START, "retrieve")
    g.add_edge("retrieve", "grade_documents")
    g.add_edge("grade_documents", "generate")
    g.add_conditional_edges("generate", check_answer,
                            {"done": END, "regenerate": "generate", "rewrite": "rewrite_query"})
    g.add_edge("rewrite_query", "retrieve")
    return g.compile()

docs.title: Agent 24 - Plan-and-Execute (LangGraph)
docs.text: Framework: LangGraph  ·  Industry: Agent Patterns  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: For multi-step tasks, a planner first writes a step-by-step plan. An executor agent (with web search) carries out one step at a time, and a re-planner looks at the results and either finishes with an answer or updates the remaining steps.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Plan first, act second: better than a single agent loop for long tasks because the plan keeps it on track.
  • Subgraph as a node: the executor is a complete tool-using agent made with create_agent from langchain.agents, called inside the execute node.
  • Accumulating state: past_steps: Annotated[list, operator.add] appends each step's result instead of overwriting.
  • Re-planning: structured output Replan either returns final_answer or remaining_steps.

docs.title: The graph
docs.text:
START -> planner -> execute -> replan --(more steps)--> execute
                                     \--(answer)--> END
MAX_STEPS = 5 caps the work.

docs.title: Known limits

  • The planner doesn't always respect "2 to 4 steps".

langgraph/24_plan_and_execute/main.py
import operator
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Annotated, TypedDict

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from ddgs import DDGS
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain_core.tools import tool
from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama
from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL

MAX_STEPS = 5
llm = ChatOllama(model=DEFAULT_MODEL, base_url=OLLAMA_URL, temperature=0)


@tool
def web_search(query: str) -> str:
    """Search the web and return short results with URLs."""
    return "\n".join(f"- {r['title']}: {r['body']} ({r['href']})" for r in DDGS().text(query, max_results=3))


class Plan(BaseModel):
    steps: list[str] = Field(description="2 to 4 short, concrete steps, in order")


class Replan(BaseModel):
    final_answer: str = Field(description="The final answer if the task is complete, otherwise empty")
    remaining_steps: list[str] = Field(description="Steps still needed, empty if the task is complete")


class State(TypedDict):
    task: str
    plan: list[str]
    past_steps: Annotated[list[tuple[str, str]], operator.add]
    answer: str


# The executor is itself a small tool-using agent (a subgraph) that handles one step at a time
executor = create_agent(llm, tools=[web_search],
                        system_prompt="Complete the given step. Use web_search for facts. Reply in under 80 words.")


def planner(state: State) -> dict:
    plan = llm.with_structured_output(Plan).invoke(f"Make a step-by-step plan for this task:\n{state['task']}")
    print("[plan]\n" + "\n".join(f"  {i}. {s}" for i, s in enumerate(plan.steps, 1)))
    return {"plan": plan.steps}


def execute(state: State) -> dict:
    step = state["plan"][0]
    done = "\n".join(f"- {s}: {r}" for s, r in state["past_steps"])
    out = executor.invoke({"messages": [("user", f"Task: {state['task']}\nDone so far:\n{done}\n\nNow do: {step}")]})
    result = out["messages"][-1].content
    print(f"\n[execute] {step}\n  -> {result[:300]}")
    return {"past_steps": [(step, result)]}


def replan(state: State) -> dict:
    done = "\n".join(f"- {s}: {r}" for s, r in state["past_steps"])
    if len(state["past_steps"]) >= MAX_STEPS:
        r = llm.invoke(f"Task: {state['task']}\nFindings:\n{done}\nWrite the final answer.").content
        return {"answer": r, "plan": []}
    r = llm.with_structured_output(Replan).invoke(
        f"Task: {state['task']}\nOriginal plan: {state['plan']}\nCompleted steps and results:\n{done}\n\n"
        "If the results are enough, give final_answer and no remaining_steps. Otherwise list remaining_steps.")
    if r.final_answer and not r.remaining_steps:
        return {"answer": r.final_answer, "plan": []}
    print(f"\n[replan] remaining: {r.remaining_steps}")
    return {"plan": r.remaining_steps or state["plan"][1:]}


def route(state: State) -> str:
    return END if state["answer"] or not state["plan"] else "execute"


def build_graph():
    g = StateGraph(State)
    g.add_node("planner", planner)
    g.add_node("execute", execute)
    g.add_node("replan", replan)
    g.add_edge(START, "planner")
    g.add_edge("planner", "execute")
    g.add_edge("execute", "replan")
    g.add_conditional_edges("replan", route, ["execute", END])
    return g.compile()


def main() -> None:
    task = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]).strip()
    if not task:
        print('Please provide a task, e.g. main.py "Who won the last FIFA World Cup and what is the captain\'s age?"')
        sys.exit(1)
    out = build_graph().invoke({"task": task, "plan": [], "past_steps": [], "answer": ""}, {"recursion_limit": 30})
    print(f"\n===== ANSWER =====\n{out['answer']}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Routes each question to the best source before answering: the company handbook (with relevance grading), a web search, or a direct answer from the model. The output shows which route was used.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Query routing: a router LLM call with structured output (Route.datasource) decides the path before any retrieval. Cheap questions ("15 times 12") skip retrieval entirely.

Listing the handbook's topics in the field description and telling the router the user is an employee fixed it.
  • Fallback inside a route: if the handbook has nothing relevant, the handbook path falls back to web search (as in Agent 13).

import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal, TypedDict

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from ddgs import DDGS
from langchain_core.vectorstores import InMemoryVectorStore
from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama, OllamaEmbeddings
from langchain_text_splitters import MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter
from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, EMBED_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL

DOCS_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "docs"
llm = ChatOllama(model=DEFAULT_MODEL, base_url=OLLAMA_URL, temperature=0)


class Route(BaseModel):
    datasource: Literal["handbook", "web_search", "direct"] = Field(
        description="handbook: anything about working here - leave, holidays, remote work, travel, meals, "
                    "expenses, allowances, passwords, security, laptops, equipment. "
                    "web_search: news, sports, prices, recent events, public facts that change. "
                    "direct: greetings, maths, stable general knowledge.")


class YesNo(BaseModel):
    score: Literal["yes", "no"]


class State(TypedDict):
    question: str
    route: str
    documents: list[str]
    answer: str


def build_store() -> InMemoryVectorStore:
    splitter = MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter([("#", "title"), ("##", "section")])
    chunks = [c for p in DOCS_DIR.glob("*.md") for c in splitter.split_text(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))]
    store = InMemoryVectorStore(OllamaEmbeddings(model=EMBED_MODEL, base_url=OLLAMA_URL))
    store.add_documents(chunks)
    return store


STORE = build_store()


def route_question(state: State) -> str:
    r = llm.with_structured_output(Route).invoke(
        "You route questions for an assistant at Acme Robotics. The user is an Acme employee, so questions about "
        f"work rules usually mean Acme's handbook.\nQuestion: {state['question']}")
    print(f"[router] -> {r.datasource}")
    return r.datasource


def retrieve(state: State) -> dict:
    docs = [d.page_content for d in STORE.similarity_search(state["question"], k=3)]
    grader = llm.with_structured_output(YesNo)
    kept = [d for d in docs if grader.invoke(
        f"Question: {state['question']}\nDocument: {d}\nIs the document relevant? yes or no.").score == "yes"]
    print(f"[handbook] {len(kept)} relevant chunks")
    return {"documents": kept, "route": "handbook"}


def after_retrieve(state: State) -> str:
    if state["documents"]:
        return "generate"
    print("[handbook] nothing relevant -> falling back to web search")
    return "web_search"


def web_search(state: State) -> dict:
    results = DDGS().text(state["question"], max_results=4)
    print(f"[web_search] {len(results)} results")
    return {"documents": [f"{r['title']}: {r['body']} ({r['href']})" for r in results], "route": "web_search"}


def generate(state: State) -> dict:
    context = "\n\n".join(state["documents"])
    answer = llm.invoke(f"Answer using only this context; cite URLs if present.\n\nContext:\n{context}\n\n"
                        f"Question: {state['question']}").content
    return {"answer": answer}


def direct(state: State) -> dict:
    return {"answer": llm.invoke(state["question"]).content, "route": "direct"}


def build_graph():
    g = StateGraph(State)
    for name, fn in [("retrieve", retrieve), ("web_search", web_search), ("generate", generate), ("direct", direct)]:
        g.add_node(name, fn)
    g.add_conditional_edges(START, route_question, {"handbook": "retrieve", "web_search": "web_search",
                                                    "direct": "direct"})
    g.add_conditional_edges("retrieve", after_retrieve, ["generate", "web_search"])
    g.add_edge("web_search", "generate")
    g.add_edge("generate", END)
    g.add_edge("direct", END)
    return g.compile()


def main() -> None:
    question = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]).strip()
    if not question:
        print("Please provide a question.")
        sys.exit(1)
    out = build_graph().invoke({"question": question, "route": "", "documents": [], "answer": ""})
    print(f"\n[source: {out['route']}]\n{out['answer']}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Agent 31 - Supervisor Multi-Agent (LangGraph)
docs.text:
Framework: LangGraph  ·  Industry: Agent Patterns  ·  Source folder on GitHub

Guardrails

This agent demonstrates guardrails. Search the code below for GUARDRAIL, and see the Guardrails overview.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: A supervisor manages three workers: a researcher (web search), an analyst (calculator) and a writer. After each worker speaks, the supervisor decides who goes next, until the writer produces the final answer.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Supervisor pattern: one LLM call with structured output (Next.next = researcher / analyst / writer / FINISH) acts as a router. Workers never talk to each other directly; everything goes through the supervisor.
  • Workers are full agents: each is built with create_agent and has its own tools and prompt.
  • Named messages: worker replies are added as HumanMessage(name=...), so the supervisor sees who said what.
  • Guardrails in code beat prompts: the researcher kept doing the maths itself even when told not to, so the analyst was never used. A rule in choose_next now forces the analyst to check the numbers before the writer may run. When a model ignores instructions, enforce the workflow in code.
  • Safe calculator: common/tools.py parses arithmetic with Python's ast instead of eval, so no code can be executed.

docs.title: Guardrails (LangChain middleware)
docs.text:
Search main.py for GUARDRAIL to find them. Every worker is built with create_agent(..., middleware=[...]):

Middleware Applied to What it does PIIMiddleware("email", strategy="redact") all workers Replaces emails in the input with [REDACTED_EMAIL] before the model sees them PIIMiddleware("credit_card", strategy="mask") all workers Masks card numbers, keeping only the last 4 digits ModelCallLimitMiddleware(run_limit=5, exit_behavior="end") all workers At most 5 model calls per worker turn: no endless loops ToolCallLimitMiddleware(tool_name="web_search", run_limit=2) researcher At most 2 searches per turn; after that the model is told the limit is reached ToolCallLimitMiddleware(tool_name="calculator", run_limit=4) analyst At most 4 calculations per turn

report_guardrails() prints a [guardrail] line whenever PII was hidden or a limit was hit. Other strategies: "block" (raise an error), "hash"; apply_to_output=True also cleans the model's replies.

Lesson from testing: PIIMiddleware only cleans the last user message. In this graph each worker's reply is added as a new message, so only the first worker got the cleaned text; the analyst, the writer and the supervisor still saw the original email and card number. The fix is a guard_input node at the start of the graph that runs the same middleware's before_model hook once on the incoming message. The cleaned message replaces the original, so nobody downstream ever sees the raw PII. Middleware protects the agent it wraps; protect the whole graph at its entry.

There is also a hand-written workflow guardrail in choose_next: the writer can't run until the analyst has checked the numbers (see below).

docs.title: The graph
docs.text:
START -> guard_input (PII) -> supervisor --> researcher --+
            ^       --> analyst    --+--> supervisor ... --> writer -> FINISH
            +------------------------+
MAX_HOPS = 6 caps the work.
