langgraph/31_supervisor_multi_agent/main.py
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.agents.middleware import ModelCallLimitMiddleware, PIIMiddleware, ToolCallLimitMiddleware
from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage
from langchain_core.tools import tool
from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama
from langgraph.graph import END, START, MessagesState, StateGraph
from pydantic import BaseModel

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL
from common.tools import calculate, web_search as _web_search

MAX_HOPS = 6
llm = ChatOllama(model=DEFAULT_MODEL, base_url=OLLAMA_URL, temperature=0)


@tool
def web_search(query: str) -> str:
    """Search the web; returns short results with URLs."""
    return _web_search(query, 3)


@tool
def calculator(expression: str) -> str:
    """Evaluate an arithmetic expression such as '(1200 * 0.15) / 3'."""
    return calculate(expression)


# ----- GUARDRAILS ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# LangChain 1.x middleware wraps an agent's model and tool calls. Each worker gets its own guardrail stack.
def guardrails(*extra) -> list:
    return [
        PIIMiddleware("email", strategy="redact"),       # emails are replaced by [REDACTED_EMAIL] in the input
        PIIMiddleware("credit_card", strategy="mask"),   # card numbers become ****-****-****-1234
        ModelCallLimitMiddleware(run_limit=5, exit_behavior="end"),  # max 5 model calls per worker turn
        *extra,
    ]


# Each worker is its own small agent with its own tools and guardrails
WORKERS = {
    "researcher": create_agent(
        llm, [web_search],
        system_prompt="You find facts on the web and report them with URLs. Never do calculations; the analyst "
                      "does the maths.",
        # max 2 searches per turn; when the limit is hit the model is told so and must answer with what it has
        middleware=guardrails(ToolCallLimitMiddleware(tool_name="web_search", run_limit=2,
                                                      exit_behavior="continue"))),
    "analyst": create_agent(
        llm, [calculator],
        system_prompt="You check and do every calculation with the calculator tool. Show the expression and "
                      "result. If no calculation is needed, say so in one line.",
        middleware=guardrails(ToolCallLimitMiddleware(tool_name="calculator", run_limit=4,
                                                      exit_behavior="continue"))),
    "writer": create_agent(
        llm, [], system_prompt="You write the final answer for the user from the team's notes. Be clear and concise.",
        middleware=guardrails()),
}


INPUT_PII = [PIIMiddleware("email", strategy="redact"), PIIMiddleware("credit_card", strategy="mask")]


def guard_input(state: MessagesState) -> dict:
    """Graph-level guardrail: clean the user's message ONCE, before the supervisor or any worker sees it.

    PIIMiddleware inside an agent only cleans the LAST user message. Here worker replies are added as new
    messages, so without this node the analyst, the writer and the supervisor still saw the original
    email and card number (found in testing). Reusing the middleware's before_model hook keeps one set of rules,
    and the cleaned message keeps its id, so it replaces the original in the graph state."""
    messages = state["messages"]
    for mw in INPUT_PII:
        update = mw.before_model({"messages": messages}, None)
        if update:
            messages = update["messages"]
    if messages[-1].content != state["messages"][-1].content:
        print(f"  [guardrail] input: PII hidden for the whole team -> {messages[-1].content[:120]!r}")
    return {"messages": messages}


def report_guardrails(name: str, messages: list) -> None:
    """Print what the middleware did during one worker turn, so the guardrails are visible."""
    for m in messages:
        text = str(m.content)
        if m.type == "human" and ("[REDACTED" in text or "****" in text):
            print(f"  [guardrail] {name}: PII hidden before the model saw it -> {text[:120]!r}")
        if m.type == "tool" and "limit" in text.lower():
            print(f"  [guardrail] {name}: tool-call limit reached -> {text[:120]!r}")
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class Next(BaseModel):
    next: Literal["researcher", "analyst", "writer", "FINISH"]
    reason: str


def supervisor(state: MessagesState) -> dict:
    return {}


def choose_next(state: MessagesState) -> str:
    hops = sum(1 for m in state["messages"] if getattr(m, "name", None) in WORKERS)
    last = state["messages"][-1]
    if getattr(last, "name", None) == "writer" or hops >= MAX_HOPS:
        return "FINISH"
    history = "\n".join(f"{getattr(m, 'name', None) or m.type}: {m.content[:400]}" for m in state["messages"])
    d = llm.with_structured_output(Next).invoke(
        "You are a supervisor managing workers: researcher (web facts), analyst (maths), writer (final answer).\n"
        "Pick the next worker. Use researcher for missing facts, analyst for calculations, "
        "and writer once the facts and numbers are ready.\n\nConversation so far:\n" + history)
    spoken = {getattr(m, "name", None) for m in state["messages"]}
    if d.next in ("writer", "FINISH") and "researcher" in spoken and "analyst" not in spoken:
        # Guardrail in code: numbers must be checked by the analyst (with the calculator) before writing
        print(f"[supervisor] wanted {d.next}, but the analyst has not verified the numbers -> analyst")
        return "analyst"
    print(f"[supervisor] -> {d.next} ({d.reason})")
    return d.next


def make_worker(name: str):
    def run(state: MessagesState) -> dict:
        out = WORKERS[name].invoke({"messages": state["messages"]})
        report_guardrails(name, out["messages"])
        content = out["messages"][-1].content
        print(f"\n[{name}] {content[:400]}")
        return {"messages": [HumanMessage(content=content, name=name)]}
    return run


def build_graph():
    g = StateGraph(MessagesState)
    g.add_node("guard_input", guard_input)  # GUARDRAIL: runs first
    g.add_node("supervisor", supervisor)
    for name in WORKERS:
        g.add_node(name, make_worker(name))
        g.add_edge(name, "supervisor")
    g.add_edge(START, "guard_input")
    g.add_edge("guard_input", "supervisor")
    g.add_conditional_edges("supervisor", choose_next, {**{n: n for n in WORKERS}, "FINISH": END})
    return g.compile()


def main() -> None:
    task = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]).strip()
    if not task:
        print('Please provide a task, e.g. main.py "What is the population of Canada and what is 2 percent of it?"')
        sys.exit(1)
    out = build_graph().invoke({"messages": [("user", task)]}, {"recursion_limit": 40})
    print(f"\n===== FINAL =====\n{out['messages'][-1].content}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Agent 35 - Reflexion Agent (LangGraph)
docs.text: Framework: LangGraph  ·  Industry: Agent Patterns  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Answers a research question, critiques its own answer (what is missing, what is superfluous), turns the critique into web searches, and rewrites the answer with the new evidence and a References line. Repeats for --iterations rounds.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Reflexion vs Reflection: Agent 08's critique only changes wording. Here the critique produces search queries, so the revision is based on new facts. Self-critique drives tool use.
  • Structured self-assessment, kept small: the answer is plain text; a separate call returns a short Critique (missing, superfluous, search_queries). The first version asked for answer + critique in one big JSON object: the 7B model got stuck emitting whitespace for 20+ minutes (blocking Ollama for every other program), and with a length cap the JSON was cut off. Keep structured outputs small.
  • Grounded revision: the revisor must cite the URLs it used.

docs.title: The graph
docs.text:
START -> draft (answer + critique + queries) -> search -> revise --(iterations left and new queries)--> search
                                                                \--(done)--> END

docs.text:

.venv-langgraph\Scripts\python.exe langgraph\35_reflexion_agent\main.py "What are the main benefits and risks of nuclear fusion energy?" --iterations 1
--iterations is clamped to 1-3. Empty question exits with code 1.

docs.title: Things to try
docs.text:
• Compare the first draft with the final answer: what did the searches add?
  • Ask about something recent, where the draft is likely out of date.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• The critique tends to ask for 3-5 searches; only the first 3 are run.
  • More iterations = more searches and a longer run.

langgraph/35_reflexion_agent/main.py
import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TypedDict

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama
from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL
from common.tools import web_search

# num_predict caps every reply. The answer is written as plain text and only the short critique is structured:
# asking for answer + critique in ONE big JSON object first got the model stuck emitting whitespace for 20+
# minutes (blocking Ollama), and with a length cap the JSON was cut off before its last fields.
llm = ChatOllama(model=DEFAULT_MODEL, base_url=OLLAMA_URL, temperature=0, num_predict=1200)


class Critique(BaseModel):
    missing: str = Field(description="What important information is missing or unverified, one sentence")
    superfluous: str = Field(description="What is unnecessary or vague, one sentence")
    search_queries: list[str] = Field(description="1-3 short web searches that would fix what is missing")


def critique(question: str, answer: str) -> Critique:
    return llm.with_structured_output(Critique).invoke(
        f"Question: {question}\n\nAnswer:\n{answer}\n\nCritique this answer honestly and propose web searches.")


class State(TypedDict):
    question: str
    answer: str
    reflection: str
    queries: list[str]
    evidence: str
    iteration: int
    max_iterations: int


def first_draft(state: State) -> dict:
    answer = llm.invoke(f"Answer in about 120 words: {state['question']}").content
    c = critique(state["question"], answer)
    print(f"\n[draft]\n{answer}\n[self-critique] missing: {c.missing}\n[queries] {c.search_queries}")
    return {"answer": answer, "reflection": c.missing, "queries": c.search_queries[:3], "iteration": 0}


def run_searches(state: State) -> dict:
    evidence = "\n\n".join(f"Search: {q}\n{web_search(q, 3)}" for q in state["queries"])
    print(f"\n[search] ran {len(state['queries'])} queries")
    return {"evidence": evidence}


def revise(state: State) -> dict:
    answer = llm.invoke(
        f"Question: {state['question']}\n\nYour previous answer:\n{state['answer']}\n\n"
        f"Your critique: {state['reflection']}\n\nNew evidence from the web:\n{state['evidence']}\n\n"
        "Rewrite the answer (about 150 words) using the evidence. End with a 'References:' line listing the "
        "URLs you used.").content
    c = critique(state["question"], answer)
    n = state["iteration"] + 1
    print(f"\n[revision {n}]\n{answer}\n[self-critique] missing: {c.missing}")
    return {"answer": answer, "reflection": c.missing, "queries": c.search_queries[:3], "iteration": n}


def keep_going(state: State) -> str:
    return "search" if state["iteration"] < state["max_iterations"] and state["queries"] else END


def build_graph():
    g = StateGraph(State)
    g.add_node("draft", first_draft)
    g.add_node("search", run_searches)
    g.add_node("revise", revise)
    g.add_edge(START, "draft")
    g.add_edge("draft", "search")
    g.add_edge("search", "revise")
    g.add_conditional_edges("revise", keep_going, ["search", END])
    return g.compile()


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="LangGraph Reflexion agent: answer, self-critique, search, revise")
    p.add_argument("question", nargs="?", default="")
    p.add_argument("--iterations", type=int, default=2)
    a = p.parse_args()
    if not a.question.strip():
        print("Please provide a question.")
        sys.exit(1)
    out = build_graph().invoke({"question": a.question.strip(), "answer": "", "reflection": "", "queries": [],
                                "evidence": "", "iteration": 0, "max_iterations": max(1, min(a.iterations, 3))})
    print(f"\n===== FINAL ANSWER =====\n{out['answer']}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Agent 38 - Customer Support with human approval (LangGraph)
docs.text: Framework: LangGraph  ·  Industry: Customer Service  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: A support chat for a fictional store (orders A100, A101, A102). Each message is classified (order status, refund, technical, other) and routed to a specialist. Order questions use a lookup tool. Refunds pause the whole graph until a human supervisor types y or n.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Router + specialists: a classify node with structured output picks the specialist node; each specialist has its own prompt and tools.
  • Human-in-the-loop with interrupt(): inside the request_refund tool, interrupt(...) pauses the graph and returns control to your program. The program asks the supervisor and resumes with graph.invoke(Command(resume="y"), config).
  • Checkpointer: InMemorySaver + a thread_id is required for interrupts and also remembers the conversation across turns.
  • Policy in code: refunds after 30 days are refused by the tool itself, before any human is asked.
  • Context-aware routing: the router sees the last few messages, so "yes" after a refund question stays a refund.

docs.title: The graph
docs.text:
START -> classify --> order_status <-> order_status_tools
                  --> refund       <-> refund_tools (request_refund: interrupt -> human y/n)
                  --> technical
                  --> other

docs.title: Agent 42 - Hierarchical Agent Teams (LangGraph)
docs.text: Framework: LangGraph  ·  Industry: Agent Patterns  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: A top-level supervisor manages two teams. The research team (searcher + fact checker) gathers and verifies facts; the writing team (writer + editor) produces the text. Each team has its own supervisor deciding which member works next.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Hierarchy = graphs inside graphs: each team is a compiled StateGraph (a subgraph). The top graph treats a whole team as one node.
  • Why hierarchies: one supervisor choosing among many workers gets confused; splitting into teams keeps each decision small.
  • Dynamic structured output: create_model(...) builds a Literal[...] type from each team's member names, so the same supervisor code works for any team.
  • Hop limits: MAX_HOPS_PER_TEAM stops a team from looping forever.

docs.title: The graph
docs.text:
top supervisor -> research_team [supervisor -> searcher | fact_checker] -> top
               -> writing_team  [supervisor -> writer | editor]         -> top -> END

docs.text:
langgraph/42_hierarchical_agent_teams/main.py
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage
from langchain_core.tools import tool
from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama
from langgraph.graph import END, START, MessagesState, StateGraph
from pydantic import BaseModel, create_model

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL
from common.tools import web_search as _web_search

llm = ChatOllama(model=DEFAULT_MODEL, base_url=OLLAMA_URL, temperature=0)
MAX_HOPS_PER_TEAM = 3


@tool
def web_search(query: str) -> str:
    """Search the web; returns short results with URLs."""
    return _web_search(query, 3)


def make_supervisor(members: list[str], job: str, max_hops: int):
    """A supervisor is an LLM call that picks the next member (or FINISH) with structured output."""
    Choice: type[BaseModel] = create_model("Choice", next=(Literal[tuple(members + ["FINISH"])], ...))

    def choose(state: MessagesState) -> str:
        hops = sum(1 for m in state["messages"] if getattr(m, "name", None) in members)
        if hops >= max_hops:
            return "FINISH"
        history = "\n".join(f"{getattr(m, 'name', None) or m.type}: {m.content[:300]}" for m in state["messages"])
        d = llm.with_structured_output(Choice).invoke(
            f"You supervise: {', '.join(members)}. {job}\nPick who acts next, or FINISH when the work is done. "
            f"Do not pick the same member twice in a row unless needed.\n\nSo far:\n{history}")
        print(f"  [{job.split('.')[0]}] -> {d.next}")
        return d.next
    return choose


def make_team(workers: dict, job: str):
    """Build one team as its own compiled graph (a subgraph)."""
    def as_node(worker_name, agent):
        def run(state: MessagesState) -> dict:
            out = agent.invoke({"messages": state["messages"]})["messages"][-1].content
            print(f"    [{worker_name}] {out[:200]}")
            return {"messages": [HumanMessage(content=out, name=worker_name)]}
        return run

    g = StateGraph(MessagesState)
    g.add_node("supervisor", lambda s: {})
    for w, agent in workers.items():
        g.add_node(w, as_node(w, agent))
        g.add_edge(w, "supervisor")
    g.add_edge(START, "supervisor")
    g.add_conditional_edges("supervisor", make_supervisor(list(workers), job, MAX_HOPS_PER_TEAM),
                            {**{w: w for w in workers}, "FINISH": END})
    return g.compile()


research_team = make_team({
    "searcher": create_agent(llm, [web_search], system_prompt="Find facts on the web. List facts with URLs."),
    "fact_checker": create_agent(llm, [web_search], system_prompt="Check the facts found so far with one more "
                                                                  "search. Say which are confirmed."),
}, "Research team. Gather and verify facts for the request.")

writing_team = make_team({
    "writer": create_agent(llm, [], system_prompt="Write the requested piece from the research notes."),
    "editor": create_agent(llm, [], system_prompt="Edit the latest draft for clarity. Cut it to the length the "
                                                  "user asked for in the first message. Return only the full "
                                                  "improved text."),
}, "Writing team. Produce and polish the final text.")


def team_node(name: str, team):
    def run(state: MessagesState) -> dict:
        print(f"\n[top supervisor] -> {name}")
        out = team.invoke({"messages": state["messages"]}, {"recursion_limit": 30})
        return {"messages": [HumanMessage(content=out["messages"][-1].content, name=name)]}
    return run


def top_choice(state: MessagesState) -> str:
    done = [getattr(m, "name", None) for m in state["messages"]]
    if "writing_team" in done:
        return "FINISH"
    TopChoice = create_model("TopChoice", next=(Literal["research_team", "writing_team", "FINISH"], ...))
    history = "\n".join(f"{getattr(m, 'name', None) or m.type}: {m.content[:300]}" for m in state["messages"])
    return llm.with_structured_output(TopChoice).invoke(
        "You lead two teams: research_team (finds facts) and writing_team (writes the text). "
        f"Research comes before writing. Pick the next team or FINISH.\n\n{history}").next


def build_graph():
    g = StateGraph(MessagesState)
    g.add_node("top", lambda s: {})
    g.add_node("research_team", team_node("research_team", research_team))
    g.add_node("writing_team", team_node("writing_team", writing_team))
    g.add_edge(START, "top")
    g.add_edge("research_team", "top")
    g.add_edge("writing_team", "top")
    g.add_conditional_edges("top", top_choice, {"research_team": "research_team", "writing_team": "writing_team",
                                                "FINISH": END})
    return g.compile()


def main() -> None:
    task = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]).strip()
    if not task:
        print('Please provide a task, e.g. main.py "Write a short blog post about the James Webb telescope"')
        sys.exit(1)
    out = build_graph().invoke({"messages": [("user", task)]}, {"recursion_limit": 30})
    print(f"\n===== FINAL =====\n{out['messages'][-1].content}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Agent 45 - Code Assistant (LangGraph)
docs.text: Framework: LangGraph  ·  Industry: Software Dev  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Describe a small coding task. The assistant writes a Python solution as structured output (approach, imports, code), the graph actually runs it, and if the imports or the code fail, the error is fed back for a fix (up to 3 attempts).

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Structured code output: Code(prefix, imports, code) separates parts so each can be checked; the import check catches missing libraries before running the full program.
  • Test-driven loop in a graph: generate -> check -> (error?) -> generate. Real execution results, not the model's opinion, decide when to stop.
  • Running code safely-ish: code runs in a separate python subprocess with a 30-second timeout and a temporary file.
  • Coder model: uses CODER_MODEL (qwen3-coder:30b) from common/llm.py.

docs.title: The graph
docs.text:
START -> generate -> check --(passed or 3 attempts)--> END
                       \--(error)--> generate (with the error message)

  • Compare with Agent 04 (AutoGen): there two agents talk; here a graph checks.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Model-written code runs on your machine (in a subprocess). Keep tasks simple and read the code.
  • "Passed" only means it ran without errors, not that the output is correct.
  • The 30B model is slow to load the first time.

langgraph/45_code_assistant/main.py
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TypedDict

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama
from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from common.llm import CODER_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL

MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3
llm = ChatOllama(model=CODER_MODEL, base_url=OLLAMA_URL, temperature=0, num_ctx=16384)


class Code(BaseModel):
    prefix: str = Field(description="One or two sentences describing the approach")
    imports: str = Field(description="Only the import statements")
    code: str = Field(description="The code without imports. It must print a demonstration of the result.")


class State(TypedDict):
    task: str
    solution: Code | None
    error: str
    attempts: int


def generate(state: State) -> dict:
    prompt = f"Write a Python 3 solution (standard library only).\nTask: {state['task']}"
    if state["error"]:
        prev = state["solution"]
        prompt += (f"\n\nYour previous attempt failed.\nImports:\n{prev.imports}\nCode:\n{prev.code}\n"
                   f"Error:\n{state['error']}\nFix it.")
    sol = llm.with_structured_output(Code).invoke(prompt)
    print(f"\n[generate] attempt {state['attempts'] + 1}: {sol.prefix}")
    return {"solution": sol, "attempts": state["attempts"] + 1, "error": ""}


def run_python(source: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".py", delete=False, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(source)
    try:
        r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, f.name], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
        return r.returncode == 0, (r.stdout if r.returncode == 0 else r.stderr)[-1500:]
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return False, "Timed out after 30 seconds."
    finally:
        Path(f.name).unlink(missing_ok=True)


def check(state: State) -> dict:
    sol = state["solution"]
    ok, out = run_python(sol.imports)
    if not ok:
        print(f"[check] import failed:\n{out}")
        return {"error": f"Import error: {out}"}
    ok, out = run_python(sol.imports + "\n\n" + sol.code)
    print(f"[check] {'passed' if ok else 'failed'}:\n{out.strip()[:800]}")
    return {"error": "" if ok else out}


def decide(state: State) -> str:
    if not state["error"] or state["attempts"] >= MAX_ATTEMPTS:
        return END
    return "generate"


def build_graph():
    g = StateGraph(State)
    g.add_node("generate", generate)
    g.add_node("check", check)
    g.add_edge(START, "generate")
    g.add_edge("generate", "check")
    g.add_conditional_edges("check", decide, ["generate", END])
    return g.compile()


def main() -> None:
    task = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]).strip()
    if not task:
        print('Please provide a coding task, e.g. main.py "A function that checks if a string is a palindrome"')
        sys.exit(1)
    out = build_graph().invoke({"task": task, "solution": None, "error": "", "attempts": 0})
    status = "WORKING" if not out["error"] else f"STILL FAILING after {out['attempts']} attempts"
    print(f"\n===== {status} =====\n{out['solution'].imports}\n\n{out['solution'].code}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Agent 49 - Information Gathering (LangGraph)
docs.text: Framework: LangGraph  ·  Industry: Customer Service  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: A chatbot that helps you design a reusable LLM prompt template. It asks questions until it knows four things (objective, variables, constraints, requirements), then generates the template with {placeholders}.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• A tool as a "form": PromptInstructions is a Pydantic model bound as a tool. The model "calls" it only when every field is known; that call is the signal that gathering is done. Nothing is executed; the arguments are the collected data.
  • Two-phase graph: gather (ask questions) and write_prompt (use the collected data). The router checks for the tool call.
  • Waiting for the user = ending the run: when the bot asks a question, the graph goes to END. The next message continues the same conversation because of the checkpointer.
  • Checkpointer memory: InMemorySaver + a thread_id keeps the conversation between turns.

docs.title: The graph
docs.text:
START -> gather --(PromptInstructions called)--> write_prompt -> END
               \--(asked a question)--> END (wait for the next user message)

langgraph/49_information_gathering/main.py
import sys
import uuid
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, ToolMessage
from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver
from langgraph.graph import END, START, MessagesState, StateGraph
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL

llm = ChatOllama(model=DEFAULT_MODEL, base_url=OLLAMA_URL, temperature=0)


class PromptInstructions(BaseModel):
    """Call this ONLY when you know all four: objective, variables, constraints and requirements."""
    objective: str = Field(description="What the prompt should achieve")
    variables: list[str] = Field(description="Inputs that will be filled into the prompt")
    constraints: list[str] = Field(description="Things the output must avoid")
    requirements: list[str] = Field(description="Things the output must do, e.g. format")


GATHER = """You help the user design a prompt template for an LLM. Ask questions, one or two at a time, until you know:
1. the objective, 2. the variables passed in, 3. constraints (what to avoid), 4. requirements (format, tone).
Do not guess missing items; ask. When you know all four, call PromptInstructions."""


def gather(state: MessagesState) -> dict:
    return {"messages": [llm.bind_tools([PromptInstructions]).invoke([("system", GATHER)] + state["messages"])]}


def route(state: MessagesState) -> Literal["write_prompt", "__end__"]:
    last = state["messages"][-1]
    return "write_prompt" if isinstance(last, AIMessage) and last.tool_calls else END  # END = wait for the user


def write_prompt(state: MessagesState) -> dict:
    call = state["messages"][-1].tool_calls[0]
    spec = PromptInstructions(**call["args"])
    print(f"\n[collected] {spec.model_dump()}")
    template = llm.invoke(
        "Write a reusable prompt template from this spec. Put each variable in {curly_braces}.\n"
        f"{spec.model_dump_json(indent=2)}").content
    return {"messages": [ToolMessage(content="Spec complete.", tool_call_id=call["id"]),
                         AIMessage(content=f"Here is your prompt template:\n\n{template}")]}


def build_graph():
    g = StateGraph(MessagesState)
    g.add_node("gather", gather)
    g.add_node("write_prompt", write_prompt)
    g.add_edge(START, "gather")
    g.add_conditional_edges("gather", route)
    g.add_edge("write_prompt", END)
    return g.compile(checkpointer=InMemorySaver())  # remembers the conversation between turns


def main() -> None:
    graph = build_graph()
    config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": str(uuid.uuid4())}}
    print("Prompt-template designer. Tell me what you want the prompt to do. Type 'exit' to quit.")
    while True:
        try:
            text = input("\nyou> ").strip()
        except EOFError:
            break
        if text.lower() in {"exit", "quit"}:
            break
        if not text:
            continue
        out = graph.invoke({"messages": [("user", text)]}, config)
        print(f"\nbot> {out['messages'][-1].content}")
        if out["messages"][-1].content.startswith("Here is your prompt template"):
            break


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.text: Framework: LangGraph  ·  Industry: Banking  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Reads a bank statement CSV (date, description, amount), categorises every transaction, computes monthly income/spend/savings and spending by category, flags unusual transactions (very large purchases, duplicate subscription charges, new large merchants), and writes a friendly report with a budget suggestion. A synthetic 3-month statement is generated on first run; it contains no real data.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Pipeline graph: a straight line of nodes (categorise -> analyse -> write_report) is still a useful LangGraph: each step is testable and the state shows what happened.
  • Rules first, LLM for the rest: known merchants are categorised by a rules table; only unknown merchants (for example "CRYPTOFX GLOBAL LTD") go to the LLM with structured output.
  • Never let the LLM do the maths: totals, medians, anomalies and even the top-3 ranking are computed in Python. In testing, the LLM picked the wrong top 3 and misread "2x" as "£2" until those were pre-computed. The LLM only explains the results.

docs.title: The graph
docs.text: CSV -> categorise (rules + LLM) -> analyse (Python maths, anomaly rules) -> write_report (LLM) -> report

import argparse
import csv
import random
import statistics
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import date, timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TypedDict

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama
from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph
from pydantic import BaseModel

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL

HERE = Path(__file__).parent
SAMPLE = HERE / "sample_statement.csv"
llm = ChatOllama(model=DEFAULT_MODEL, base_url=OLLAMA_URL, temperature=0)

# Known merchants are categorised by rules; unknown ones go to the LLM
RULES = {"TESCO": "Groceries", "LIDL": "Groceries", "ALDI": "Groceries", "SHELL": "Transport", "UBER": "Transport",
         "TFL": "Transport", "NETFLIX": "Subscriptions", "SPOTIFY": "Subscriptions", "RENT": "Housing",
         "BRITISH GAS": "Utilities", "THAMES WATER": "Utilities", "SALARY": "Income", "PRET": "Eating out",
         "DELIVEROO": "Eating out", "AMAZON": "Shopping"}


def make_sample(path: Path) -> None:
    """Synthetic statement for 3 months, with a few planted oddities. Not real data."""
    rng = random.Random(7)
    rows = []
    for month in (6, 7, 8):
        m0 = date(2026, month, 1)
        rows += [(m0, "SALARY ACME LTD", 3200.00), (m0 + timedelta(days=1), "RENT PAYMENT", -1250.00),
                 (m0 + timedelta(days=3), "BRITISH GAS", -85.40), (m0 + timedelta(days=5), "NETFLIX", -10.99),
                 (m0 + timedelta(days=5), "SPOTIFY", -11.99), (m0 + timedelta(days=9), "THAMES WATER", -38.00),
                 (m0 + timedelta(days=2), "CITY GYM", -35.00)]
        for _ in range(22):
            merchant, low, high = rng.choice([("TESCO", 12, 70), ("LIDL", 8, 45), ("PRET", 4, 12),
                                              ("UBER", 8, 25), ("TFL", 3, 9), ("AMAZON", 10, 60),
                                              ("DELIVEROO", 15, 35), ("BOOTS PHARMACY", 5, 25)])
            rows.append((m0 + timedelta(days=rng.randint(0, 28)), merchant, -round(rng.uniform(low, high), 2)))
    rows += [(date(2026, 7, 14), "AMAZON", -899.00),                    # unusually large
             (date(2026, 8, 2), "NETFLIX", -10.99),                     # duplicate charge in the same month
             (date(2026, 8, 19), "CRYPTOFX GLOBAL LTD", -450.00),       # new unknown merchant
             (date(2026, 8, 20), "CRYPTOFX GLOBAL LTD", -450.00)]
    rows.sort()
    with open(path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.writer(f)
        w.writerow(["date", "description", "amount"])
        w.writerows((d.isoformat(), desc, f"{amt:.2f}") for d, desc, amt in rows)


class Categories(BaseModel):
    mapping: dict[str, str]


class State(TypedDict):
    rows: list[dict]
    findings: dict
    report: str


def load(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return [{"date": r["date"], "description": r["description"].upper(), "amount": float(r["amount"])}
                for r in csv.DictReader(f)]


def categorise(state: State) -> dict:
    unknown = sorted({r["description"] for r in state["rows"]
                      if not any(k in r["description"] for k in RULES)})
    llm_map = {}
    if unknown:
        llm_map = llm.with_structured_output(Categories).invoke(
            "Assign each bank-statement merchant one category from: Groceries, Transport, Subscriptions, "
            "Housing, Utilities, Eating out, Shopping, Health & Fitness, Investments, Other. "
            f"Return a mapping merchant -> category.\nMerchants: {unknown}").mapping
        print(f"[categorise] LLM labelled {len(llm_map)} unknown merchants: {llm_map}")
    for r in state["rows"]:
        rule = next((cat for key, cat in RULES.items() if key in r["description"]), None)
        r["category"] = rule or llm_map.get(r["description"], "Other")
    return {"rows": state["rows"]}


def analyse(state: State) -> dict:
    """Plain Python does the maths; the LLM never calculates totals."""
    spend, months, by_merchant = defaultdict(float), defaultdict(lambda: [0.0, 0.0]), defaultdict(list)
    for r in state["rows"]:
        m = r["date"][:7]
        if r["amount"] > 0:
            months[m][0] += r["amount"]
        else:
            months[m][1] += -r["amount"]
            spend[r["category"]] += -r["amount"]
            by_merchant[r["description"]].append(r)
    unusual = []
    for merchant, rs in by_merchant.items():
        amounts = [-r["amount"] for r in rs]
        med = statistics.median(amounts)
        unusual += [f"{r['date']} {merchant} {-r['amount']:.2f} (typical {med:.2f})"
                    for r in rs if len(rs) >= 3 and -r["amount"] > 4 * med]
        if len(rs) <= 2 and min(amounts) >= 200:
            unusual.append(f"New large merchant: {merchant}, {len(rs)} payments totalling {sum(amounts):.2f}")
        seen = defaultdict(int)
        for r in rs:
            seen[(r["date"][:7], r["amount"])] += 1
        if merchant in ("NETFLIX", "SPOTIFY") or any(k in merchant for k in ("GYM",)):
            unusual += [f"Possible duplicate subscription: {merchant} charged {n} times in {k[0]}"
                        for k, n in seen.items() if n > 1]
    findings = {
        "monthly": {m: {"in": round(v[0], 2), "out": round(v[1], 2), "saved": round(v[0] - v[1], 2)}
                    for m, v in sorted(months.items())},
        "spend_by_category": dict(sorted(((k, round(v, 2)) for k, v in spend.items()), key=lambda x: -x[1])),
        "top_3_categories": [k for k, _ in sorted(spend.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])[:3]],
        "best_saving_month": max(months, key=lambda m: months[m][0] - months[m][1]),
        "worst_saving_month": min(months, key=lambda m: months[m][0] - months[m][1]),
        "unusual": unusual,
    }
    print(f"[analyse] {findings}")
    return {"findings": findings}


def write_report(state: State) -> dict:
    report = llm.invoke(
        "You are a friendly personal-finance assistant. Using ONLY these computed figures (do not recalculate), "
        "write: 1) a 3-sentence overview naming best_saving_month and worst_saving_month as given, "
        "2) the top_3_categories exactly as listed, with amounts, 3) each unusual transaction and what "
        "the user should check, 4) a simple monthly budget suggestion with 3 concrete savings tips. "
        "Use the currency GBP.\n\n" + str(state["findings"])).content
    return {"report": report}


def build_graph():
    g = StateGraph(State)
    g.add_node("categorise", categorise)
    g.add_node("analyse", analyse)
    g.add_node("write_report", write_report)
    g.add_edge(START, "categorise")
    g.add_edge("categorise", "analyse")
    g.add_edge("analyse", "write_report")
    g.add_edge("write_report", END)
    return g.compile()


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="LangGraph bank statement analyst (synthetic data)")
    p.add_argument("csv", nargs="?", default=str(SAMPLE), help="CSV with columns date, description, amount")
    a = p.parse_args()
    path = Path(a.csv)
    if path == SAMPLE and not SAMPLE.exists():
        make_sample(SAMPLE)
    if not path.is_file():
        print(f"File not found: {path}")
        sys.exit(1)
    rows = load(path)
    if not rows:
        print("The statement has no transactions.")
        sys.exit(1)
    out = build_graph().invoke({"rows": rows, "findings": {}, "report": ""})
    print(f"\n===== REPORT =====\n{out['report']}\n\nEducational tool only; not financial advice.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Agent 05 - Document Q&A (LlamaIndex)
docs.text: Framework: LlamaIndex  ·  Industry: Knowledge & RAG  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Ask a question about the files in a folder. It finds the most relevant passages, answers from them only, and lists which files and how strongly each matched. Two sample documents are included (a battery manual and cafe staff notes); point --docs at your own folder to use real files.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• LlamaIndex model: it is a data framework for RAG. You load documents, build an index, then ask the index questions. No agent loop is needed.
  • Pipeline: load, split into chunks, embed, store in a vector index, retrieve top matches, send them with the question to the LLM.
  • Query engine: index.as_query_engine() bundles retrieval and answering in one object.
  • Postprocessors: the SimilarityPostprocessor drops weak matches before they reach the LLM.
  • Prompt control: a custom QA prompt forces "answer only from the context".
  • Compare with Agent 02: there retrieval was a tool the LLM chose to call (agentic). Here retrieval always runs first (classic RAG), which is simpler and more predictable.

docs.title: The flow
docs.text:
documents -> chunks -> embeddings -> VectorStoreIndex (in memory)
question -> embed -> top 3 chunks -> drop score < 0.3 -> LLM answers from them -> answer + sources
                                            \--> nothing left? "I could not find this in the documents."

docs.title: How the code works (main.py)
docs.text:
1. Settings.llm / Settings.embed_model set LlamaIndex to use local Ollama (common/llm.py) instead of its OpenAI default.
  2. SimpleDirectoryReader loads every file in the folder (txt, md, pdf and more).
  3. VectorStoreIndex.from_documents chunks, embeds and indexes them. Rebuilt each run.
  4. as_query_engine(similarity_top_k=3, node_postprocessors=[...], text_qa_template=QA_PROMPT) retrieves, filters, and answers.
  5. Sources come from response.source_nodes with their file names and scores.

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from llama_index.core import PromptTemplate, Settings, SimpleDirectoryReader, VectorStoreIndex
from llama_index.core.postprocessor import SimilarityPostprocessor
from llama_index.embeddings.ollama import OllamaEmbedding
from llama_index.llms.ollama import Ollama

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, EMBED_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL

DEFAULT_DOCS = Path(__file__).parent / "docs"
MIN_SCORE = 0.3  # chunks less similar than this are dropped before answering

QA_PROMPT = PromptTemplate(
    "Context from the user's documents:\n{context_str}\n\n"
    "Answer the question using ONLY the context above. "
    "If the context does not contain the answer, reply exactly: "
    "I could not find this in the documents.\n"
    "Question: {query_str}\nAnswer:"
)


def build_query_engine(docs_dir: Path):
    Settings.llm = Ollama(model=DEFAULT_MODEL, base_url=OLLAMA_URL, request_timeout=180, temperature=0)
    Settings.embed_model = OllamaEmbedding(model_name=EMBED_MODEL, base_url=OLLAMA_URL)
    documents = SimpleDirectoryReader(str(docs_dir)).load_data()
    index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(documents)
    return index.as_query_engine(
        similarity_top_k=3,
        node_postprocessors=[SimilarityPostprocessor(similarity_cutoff=MIN_SCORE)],
        text_qa_template=QA_PROMPT,
    )


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="LlamaIndex document Q&A")
    p.add_argument("question", nargs="?", default="")
    p.add_argument("--docs", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_DOCS, help="folder with .txt/.md/.pdf files")
    a = p.parse_args()
    if not a.question.strip():
        print("Please provide a question.")
        sys.exit(1)
    if not a.docs.is_dir() or not any(a.docs.iterdir()):
        print(f"No documents found in {a.docs}")
        sys.exit(1)

    response = build_query_engine(a.docs).query(a.question.strip())
    if not response.source_nodes:  # nothing passed the similarity cutoff
        print("\nI could not find this in the documents.")
        return
    print("\n" + str(response))
    print("\nSources:")
    for n in response.source_nodes:
        print(f"- {n.node.metadata.get('file_name', '?')} (score {n.score:.2f})")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import argparse
import csv
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from llama_index.core import SQLDatabase
from llama_index.core.query_engine import NLSQLTableQueryEngine
from sqlalchemy import Column, Float, Integer, MetaData, String, Table, create_engine, insert

from common.llamaindex_setup import use_ollama

DEFAULT_CSV = Path(__file__).parent / "sales.csv"


def csv_to_sqlite(path: Path, table: str = "sales"):
    """Load a CSV into an in-memory SQLite table, guessing INTEGER / REAL / TEXT per column."""
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
    if not rows:
        raise ValueError("CSV has no rows")

    def kind(col):
        vals = [r[col] for r in rows]
        for typ, cast in ((Integer, int), (Float, float)):
            try:
                [cast(v) for v in vals]
                return typ, cast
            except ValueError:
                pass
        return String, str

    kinds = {c: kind(c) for c in rows[0]}
    engine = create_engine("sqlite://")
    meta = MetaData()
    t = Table(table, meta, *[Column(c, k[0]) for c, k in kinds.items()])
    meta.create_all(engine)
    with engine.begin() as con:
        con.execute(insert(t), [{c: kinds[c][1](r[c]) for c in r} for r in rows])
    return engine


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="LlamaIndex natural-language questions over a CSV (text-to-SQL)")
    p.add_argument("question", nargs="?", default="")
    p.add_argument("--csv", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_CSV)
    a = p.parse_args()
    if not a.question.strip():
        print('Please ask a question, e.g. main.py "Which region had the highest revenue?"')
        sys.exit(1)
    if not a.csv.is_file():
        print(f"CSV not found: {a.csv}")
        sys.exit(1)
    use_ollama()
    db = SQLDatabase(csv_to_sqlite(a.csv), include_tables=["sales"])
    # The engine shows the LLM the table schema, asks it for SQL, runs the SQL, then writes an answer from the rows
    engine = NLSQLTableQueryEngine(sql_database=db, tables=["sales"])
    response = engine.query(a.question.strip() + " (revenue = units * unit_price)")
    print(f"\nSQL: {response.metadata.get('sql_query', '?')}\n\n{response}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

            VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(docs).as_query_engine(similarity_top_k=2),
            name=f"{city}_facts",
            description=f"Specific facts about {city.replace('_', ' ').title()}: prices, transport, food, sights."))
        tools.append(QueryEngineTool.from_defaults(
            SummaryIndex.from_documents(docs).as_query_engine(response_mode="tree_summarize"),
            name=f"{city}_summary",
            description=f"A general overview of {city.replace('_', ' ').title()} for broad questions."))

docs.title: Agent 30 - Sub-Question Query Engine (LlamaIndex)
docs.text: Framework: LlamaIndex  ·  Industry: Knowledge & RAG  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Answers comparison questions across two company reports (Northwind and Fresco; fictional 2025 summaries). It breaks your question into one sub-question per company and topic, answers each from the right document, then combines them.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Query decomposition: SubQuestionQueryEngine asks the LLM to produce sub-questions, each tagged with the tool (document) that should answer it. With verbose=True you see every sub-question and its answer.
  • Why it helps: a plain RAG search for "compare revenue growth of A and B" often retrieves only one company's text; splitting guarantees both are looked up.
  • Same tools, different engine: the per-document QueryEngineTools look like Agent 20's, but here a fixed decompose-then-merge pipeline replaces the agent's free choice.
  • Works with any LLM: SubQuestionQueryEngine.from_defaults tries to load an OpenAI-specific question generator by default and fails without that package. Passing question_gen=LLMQuestionGenerator.from_defaults() uses a plain prompt instead, which works with Ollama.

docs.title: The flow
docs.text: question -> LLM writes sub-questions -> [northwind tool, fresco tool, ...] -> sub-answers -> combined answer

from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from llama_index.core import SimpleDirectoryReader, VectorStoreIndex
from llama_index.core.query_engine import SubQuestionQueryEngine
from llama_index.core.question_gen import LLMQuestionGenerator
from llama_index.core.tools import QueryEngineTool

from common.llamaindex_setup import use_ollama

DOCS = Path(__file__).parent / "docs"


def build_engine() -> SubQuestionQueryEngine:
    tools = []
    for path in sorted(DOCS.glob("*.md")):
        company = path.stem.split("_")[0]
        index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(SimpleDirectoryReader(input_files=[str(path)]).load_data())

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from llama_index.core import SimpleDirectoryReader, SummaryIndex
from llama_index.core.node_parser import SentenceSplitter

from common.llamaindex_setup import use_ollama

DEFAULT_REPORT = Path(__file__).parent / "sample_report.md"

QUESTIONS = {
    "Executive summary": "Write a 5-sentence executive summary of the whole report for a busy decision maker.",
    "Key numbers": "List the 6 most important numbers in the report, one bullet each with what they mean.",
    "Recommendations and deadlines": "List the recommendations and any deadlines or time-critical decisions.",
    "Risks and open problems": "List the main problems or risks the report identifies, one bullet each.",
}


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="LlamaIndex long-report summarizer")
    p.add_argument("file", nargs="?", default=str(DEFAULT_REPORT), help="a .md, .txt or .pdf report")
    a = p.parse_args()
    path = Path(a.file)
    if not path.is_file():
        print(f"File not found: {path}")
        sys.exit(1)
    use_ollama()
    docs = SimpleDirectoryReader(input_files=[str(path)]).load_data()
    # Small chunks so the summary has to combine many pieces: tree_summarize summarises chunks in groups,
    # then summarises the summaries, so it works even when the report is longer than the model's context
    index = SummaryIndex.from_documents(docs, transformations=[SentenceSplitter(chunk_size=400, chunk_overlap=40)])
    engine = index.as_query_engine(response_mode="tree_summarize")
    print(f"Summarising {path.name} ({len(index.docstore.docs)} chunks)\n")
    for title, question in QUESTIONS.items():
        print(f"===== {title} =====\n{engine.query(question)}\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: What it does

"""A tiny MCP server that manages notes in a JSON file. Any MCP client (Agno, LangGraph, Claude Code, ...) can use it.

Run directly to check it starts:  python notes_mcp_server.py   (it then waits for a client on stdin/stdout)
"""
import json
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

try:  # mcp 1.x
    from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP as Server
except ImportError:  # mcp 2.x renamed FastMCP to MCPServer
    from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer as Server

NOTES = Path(__file__).parent / "notes.json"
server = Server("notes")


def _load() -> list[dict]:
    return json.loads(NOTES.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if NOTES.exists() else []


def _save(notes: list[dict]) -> None:
    NOTES.write_text(json.dumps(notes, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")


@server.tool()
def add_note(title: str, text: str, tags: list[str] | None = None) -> str:
    """Save a new note with a title, text and optional tags."""
    notes = _load()
    note = {"id": len(notes) + 1, "title": title, "text": text, "tags": tags or [],
            "created": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="minutes")}
    notes.append(note)
    _save(notes)
    return f"Saved note {note['id']}: {title}"


@server.tool()
def list_notes() -> str:
    """List all notes (id, title, tags)."""
    notes = _load()
    return "\n".join(f"{n['id']}. {n['title']} {n['tags']}" for n in notes) or "No notes yet."


@server.tool()
def search_notes(query: str) -> str:
    """Find notes whose title, text or tags contain the query (case-insensitive)."""
    q = query.lower()
    hits = [n for n in _load() if q in n["title"].lower() or q in n["text"].lower()
            or any(q in t.lower() for t in n["tags"])]
    return "\n\n".join(f"{n['id']}. {n['title']}\n{n['text']}" for n in hits) or f"No notes match '{query}'."


@server.tool()
def delete_note(note_id: int) -> str:
    """Delete a note by its id."""
    notes = _load()
    kept = [n for n in notes if n["id"] != note_id]
    if len(kept) == len(notes):
        return f"No note with id {note_id}."
    _save(kept)
    return f"Deleted note {note_id}."


if __name__ == "__main__":
    server.run()  # default transport: stdio

docs.text: Framework: Agno + A2A  ·  Industry: Protocols  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Exposes an Agno research agent (like agent 01) through the A2A (Agent2Agent) protocol, so other agents, in any framework or language, can discover it and send it tasks. Agent 55 is a client for it. It uses the shared common/tools.py web search, which retries other search backends; Agno's built-in DuckDuckGo tool crashed the request when the search returned no results.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Agent card: a public JSON "business card" at /.well-known/agent-card.json with the agent's name, description, skills, examples and endpoint. Other agents read it to decide whether and how to call this one.
  • AgentExecutor: the bridge between the protocol and your agent. execute() reads the incoming message (context.get_user_input()), runs the Agno agent, and puts a reply message on the event_queue.
  • Request handler + routes: DefaultRequestHandler (with an in-memory task store) handles the JSON-RPC methods; create_agent_card_routes and create_jsonrpc_routes turn it into a Starlette web app served by uvicorn.
  • MCP vs A2A: MCP exposes tools (the caller does the thinking). A2A exposes an agent (the remote side does its own reasoning, may take time, and can manage long tasks).

"""A2A server: exposes the Agno research agent (agent 01) so that other agents can discover and call it."""
import argparse
import asyncio
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

import uvicorn
from a2a.helpers.proto_helpers import new_text_message
from a2a.server.agent_execution import AgentExecutor, RequestContext
from a2a.server.events import EventQueue
from a2a.server.request_handlers import DefaultRequestHandler
from a2a.server.routes.agent_card_routes import create_agent_card_routes
from a2a.server.routes.jsonrpc_routes import create_jsonrpc_routes
from a2a.server.tasks import InMemoryTaskStore
from a2a.types import AgentCapabilities, AgentCard, AgentInterface, AgentSkill
from a2a.utils import DEFAULT_RPC_URL, TransportProtocol
from agno.agent import Agent
from agno.models.ollama import Ollama
from starlette.applications import Starlette

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL
from common.tools import web_search


def build_agent() -> Agent:
    return Agent(
        model=Ollama(id=DEFAULT_MODEL, host=OLLAMA_URL),
        tools=[web_search],
        instructions=["Search the web before answering.", "Answer in 5 bullet points.",
                      "End with a 'Sources:' list of full URLs."],
    )


class ResearchExecutor(AgentExecutor):
    """Bridges A2A requests to the Agno agent: read the incoming text, run the agent, send back a message."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.agent = build_agent()

    async def execute(self, context: RequestContext, event_queue: EventQueue) -> None:
        question = context.get_user_input()
        print(f"[a2a] received: {question!r}")
        result = await asyncio.to_thread(self.agent.run, question)  # Agno's run() is blocking
        await event_queue.enqueue_event(
            new_text_message(str(result.content), context_id=context.context_id, task_id=context.task_id))
        print("[a2a] answered")

    async def cancel(self, context: RequestContext, event_queue: EventQueue) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError("cancel is not supported")


def agent_card(port: int) -> AgentCard:
    """The agent card is the public 'business card' other agents download to learn what this agent can do."""
    return AgentCard(
        name="Local Research Agent",
        description="Searches the web and answers questions in 5 cited bullet points. Runs on local Ollama.",
        version="1.0.0",
        supported_interfaces=[AgentInterface(url=f"http://localhost:{port}{DEFAULT_RPC_URL}",
                                             protocol_binding=TransportProtocol.JSONRPC.value)],
        capabilities=AgentCapabilities(streaming=False),
        default_input_modes=["text/plain"],
        default_output_modes=["text/plain"],
        skills=[AgentSkill(id="web_research", name="Web research",
                           description="Answer a factual question using a web search, with sources.",
                           tags=["research", "search", "facts"],
                           examples=["What is retrieval augmented generation?", "Who won the last World Cup?"])],
    )


def build_app(port: int) -> Starlette:
    card = agent_card(port)
    handler = DefaultRequestHandler(agent_executor=ResearchExecutor(), task_store=InMemoryTaskStore(),
                                    agent_card=card)
    return Starlette(routes=create_agent_card_routes(card) + create_jsonrpc_routes(handler, DEFAULT_RPC_URL))


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="A2A server for the research agent")
    p.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=9999)
    a = p.parse_args()
    print(f"Agent card: http://localhost:{a.port}/.well-known/agent-card.json")
    uvicorn.run(build_app(a.port), host="127.0.0.1", port=a.port, log_level="warning")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Agent 55 (extra) - Planner agent as an A2A client (LangGraph)
docs.text: Framework: LangGraph + A2A  ·  Industry: Protocols  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: A LangGraph planner that does no research itself. It discovers the research agent (agent 54) from its agent card, sends it each research question over A2A, and writes the final answer from the replies. Two agents in two different frameworks (LangGraph and Agno) cooperate through the protocol.

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Discovery: the client first downloads /.well-known/agent-card.json and prints the remote agent's name and skills.
  • Sending a task: create_client(SERVER) resolves the card and picks a transport; client.send_message(SendMessageRequest(message=new_text_message(...))) returns a stream of responses; get_stream_response_text extracts the text.
  • Delegation as a graph node: the delegate node is async and calls the remote agent; the rest of the graph doesn't know or care that the work happened elsewhere.

docs.title: The graph
docs.text: START -> plan (2 questions) -> delegate (A2A calls to agent 54) -> write -> END

docs.text:
Terminal 1: start agent 54.

Terminal 2: 
cd 50-agents-for-all

If the server isn't running it prints how to start it and exits with code 1. Empty goal exits with code 1.

docs.title: Things to try
docs.text:
• Run agent 54 on another computer on your network and change SERVER.
  • Ask the questions in parallel with asyncio.gather.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• In testing the planner often returned an empty question list, so the code falls back to sending the whole goal as one question; without that fallback it silently answered from its own memory and never called the remote agent.
  • The client uses a 300-second HTTP timeout because the remote agent searches and runs a local LLM; the default timeout failed.
  • A new client per question (simple, slightly slower).

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
protocols/55_planner_a2a_client/main.py
"""A2A client: a LangGraph planner that discovers the research agent (54) by its agent card and delegates to it."""
import asyncio
import operator
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Annotated, TypedDict

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

import httpx
from a2a.client import ClientConfig, create_client
from a2a.helpers.proto_helpers import get_stream_response_text, new_text_message
from a2a.types import Role, SendMessageRequest
from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama
from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from common.llm import DEFAULT_MODEL, OLLAMA_URL

SERVER = "http://localhost:9999"
llm = ChatOllama(model=DEFAULT_MODEL, base_url=OLLAMA_URL, temperature=0)


class Questions(BaseModel):
    questions: list[str] = Field(description="2 short factual research questions")


class State(TypedDict):
    goal: str
    questions: list[str]
    answers: Annotated[list[str], operator.add]
    report: str


async def ask_remote_agent(question: str) -> str:
    """Send one question to the remote A2A agent and collect its text reply."""
    # The remote agent searches the web and runs a local LLM, which takes longer than httpx's default timeout
    config = ClientConfig(httpx_client=httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=300))
    client = await create_client(SERVER, client_config=config)  # reads the agent card, picks a transport
    request = SendMessageRequest(message=new_text_message(question, role=Role.ROLE_USER))
    parts = [get_stream_response_text(r) async for r in client.send_message(request)]
    await client.close()
    return "\n".join(p for p in parts if p)


def plan(state: State) -> dict:
    q = llm.with_structured_output(Questions).invoke(f"Goal: {state['goal']}\nWhat 2 facts do we need to look up?")
    # In testing the model sometimes returned an empty list, so the planner skipped the remote agent entirely
    # and answered from memory. Falling back to the goal itself guarantees at least one A2A call.
    questions = [x for x in q.questions if x.strip()][:2] or [state["goal"]]
    print("[planner] questions:", questions)
    return {"questions": questions}


async def delegate(state: State) -> dict:
    answers = []
    for question in state["questions"]:
        print(f"\n[planner -> research agent via A2A] {question}")
        reply = await ask_remote_agent(question)
        print(f"[research agent] {reply[:400]}")
        answers.append(f"Q: {question}\nA: {reply}")
    return {"answers": answers}


def write(state: State) -> dict:
    report = llm.invoke(f"Goal: {state['goal']}\nResearch from a partner agent:\n" + "\n\n".join(state["answers"])
                        + "\n\nWrite a short, clear answer to the goal (under 150 words) and keep the source URLs.")
    return {"report": report.content}


def build_graph():
    g = StateGraph(State)
    g.add_node("plan", plan)
    g.add_node("delegate", delegate)
    g.add_node("write", write)
    g.add_edge(START, "plan")
    g.add_edge("plan", "delegate")
    g.add_edge("delegate", "write")
    g.add_edge("write", END)
    return g.compile()


async def run(goal: str) -> None:
    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as http:  # show discovery: read the remote agent's card first
        card = (await http.get(f"{SERVER}/.well-known/agent-card.json", timeout=5)).json()
    print(f"Discovered agent: {card['name']} - skills: {[s['name'] for s in card.get('skills', [])]}\n")
    out = await build_graph().ainvoke({"goal": goal, "questions": [], "answers": [], "report": ""})
    print(f"\n===== FINAL =====\n{out['report']}")


def main() -> None:
    goal = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]).strip()
    if not goal:
        print('Please give a goal, e.g. main.py "Should I visit Iceland in winter or summer?"')
        sys.exit(1)
    try:
        asyncio.run(run(goal))
    except httpx.ConnectError:
        print(f"Cannot reach the A2A server at {SERVER}. Start it first:\n"
              r"  .venv-agno\Scripts\python.exe protocols\54_research_a2a_server\server.py")
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Agent 56 (extra) - Research Agent as a REST API (FastAPI)
docs.text: Framework: Agno + FastAPI  ·  Industry: Protocols  ·  Source folder on GitHub

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Serves a research agent (like agent 01, but with the shared common/tools.py web search, which retries other search backends) over HTTP so any program can use it: a website, a mobile app, a script in another language, or curl.

Endpoint Returns GET /health {"status": "ok", "model": ...} POST /ask {"question": "..."} JSON {"answer", "model", "tools_used"} POST /ask/stream {"question": "..."} Server-Sent Events: the answer token by token GET /docs Interactive API docs generated by FastAPI

docs.title: Concepts you learn
docs.text:
• Request/response models: Pydantic AskRequest validates input (3-500 characters) and FastAPI returns a clear 422 error otherwise.
  • Blocking work in an API: the endpoints are plain def, so FastAPI runs each request in a worker thread and the server stays responsive.
  • Streaming with SSE: run(..., stream=True) yields chunks; each is sent as a data: event (JSON-encoded, because raw newlines are not allowed inside an SSE data line).
  • One agent per request: requests don't share conversation history.

docs.title: Protocols: MCP, A2A, REST
docs.text:
How agents connect to the outside world: MCP serves tools to any agent, A2A lets agents discover and call other agents, and a REST API lets any program call an agent.

# Agent Industry What it does 52 Notes MCP: Agno client Protocols Agent uses tools from a local MCP server (notes_mcp_server.py) 53 Notes MCP: LangGraph client Protocols The same MCP server used from a second framework 54 Research Agent as A2A Server Protocols Publishes an agent card and answers A2A requests 55 Planner as A2A Client Protocols Discovers agent 54 and delegates research to it 56 Research Agent REST API Protocols /ask (JSON) and /ask/stream (SSE) endpoints

These extras take agents from the main 50 and connect them in three standard ways.

Protocol Connects Folder MCP (Model Context Protocol) an agent to tools and data served by a separate process 52 (Agno client), 53 (LangGraph client), shared server notes_mcp_server.py A2A (Agent2Agent) an agent to another agent, discovered through its agent card 54 (server), 55 (client) REST API any program to an agent over plain HTTP 56

Rule of thumb: MCP = agent to tools, A2A = agent to agent, REST = anything to agent.

The folder is called protocols/ (not mcp/ or a2a/) so it cannot be confused with the installed mcp and a2a Python packages.
